He glances through his notification centre; a handful of messages in the drivers’ association
group chat, George having sent in a fifty-one-page PDF containing the minutes from some
FIA meeting concerning next year’s regulations, to which Max Verstappen had, of course,
immediately replied that absolutely nobody has time to read all that and George should just
give them the fucking TLDR instead.
Lando is half tempted to read the entire document purely out of spite; though there is,
admittedly, a reason he never finished secondary school and instead ended up driving cars
professionally.
He scrolls further down – but there’s nothing from Discord, nothing from Oscar.
He knows they’re scheduled to meet at five p.m. his time for their first streamed training
session, but it seems Oscar is either still asleep or currently experiencing such profound
regret over everything he divulged during yesterday’s marathon call that he’s considering
deleting himself from the internet altogether.
Lando picks up his phone and scrolls absently through the rest of his notifications as he
wanders over toward the mirrored wall stretching across one side of the gym. He swaps to the
camera app and looks at himself through the lens, reflected back at him through the vast
emptiness of the room.
He looks properly undone.

Sweat gleams across every inch of exposed tan skin; his hair damp enough now to border on
wet, the McLaren shirt clinging soaked to his body. His cheeks are flushed, his face still
faintly red in that way that unmistakably betrays the past hour.
Lando snaps the picture.
He checks it over immediately, assessing whether he looks stupid; but no – he thinks he
actually looks good. Trained. Strong. Like the workout has only tempered him further.
Without thinking much about it, he posts the photo to his public Instagram story.
No rest for the wicked, he types in the default font, plastering it across the image while also
tagging the gym like his social media rep is constantly telling him to do.
He uploads the story, dumps his phone back into the pocket of his shorts, and takes an
enormous sip from his water bottle before turning toward Max, who is still scrolling on his
phone nearby.
A chime sounds. Max taps his screen and tilts his head slightly, clearly opening Lando’s
story.
Ha. This loser has his story notifications turned on.
“Who are we thirst trapping?” he asks after a moment, thumb still pressed against the screen
to hold the story in place while he looks up at Lando as he walks over.
Lando drops down beside him onto the smooth floorboards, immediately propping himself
against Max’s leg, who instinctively shoves him away with visible horror the second the
sweat-soaked fabric of Lando’s shirt touches his bare skin.
“What do you mean?” Lando says, reaching for the towel hanging from Max’s bag and
threading it through his damp hair. “This is about asserting dominance and showing the rest
of the grid that I’m actively in the gym while they’re off rotting on yachts somewhere.”
Max merely raises his eyebrows. “You’re whoring yourself out, Norris. Don’t even pretend
otherwise.”
He tilts his phone screen so Lando can see the story again. 
“Look at this. Tiny little waist on full display, sweaty as hell, bedroom eyes dialled up to the
fucking maximum.” Max clicks his tongue, looking at him with the exhausted
disappointment of a father. “Shameless.”
“That’s just what I look like,” Lando protests, though seeing the story again reflected through
Max’s phone screen, he does suddenly realise he looks considerably better than he originally
thought.
At the time he’d posted it (twenty seconds ago), he’d assumed it was simply a post-workout
picture – sweaty, exhausted, and just vaguely disgusting – but now that he’s looking at it
properly, he can already envision the image circulating around Twitter within the next few

hours accompanied by increasingly unhinged captions that, embarrassingly enough, always
make him giggle a little.
His phone vibrates suddenly against his thigh. Lando twists awkwardly to retrieve it from the
pocket of his shorts.
Magui has texted him in all caps.
 

Magui Corceiro
WHO IS HE?

 
Lando stares at the message for a moment, utterly befuddled.
 

Lando Norris
who’s who?
 
Magui Corceiro
the MAN YOU’RE WHORING YOURSELF OUT FOR ON YOUR INSTA STORY.
Chuchu, bffr.

 
Lando scoffs, unable to suppress the delighted grin tugging at the corner of his mouth. “Does
everybody in my life have my story notifications turned on?”
Max attempts to sneak a glance at his screen. “Magui?” He leans farther away again,
dragging his leg with him in another attempt to escape Lando’s sweatiness. “I have your story
notifications turned on exclusively so I can prevent any future posting mishaps on your part.
You remember lube-gate. We do not need a repeat of lube-gate.”
Lando places a sweaty hand onto Max’s knee and pinches his skin viciously.
“Dearest Max,” he says solemnly, “what would I do without you?”
Max merely purses his lips as though the answer is both devastatingly obvious and entirely
unnecessary to verbalise between them.
His phone vibrates against his leg again.
 

Magui Corceiro
Chuchuuuu please tell me pleaaaase.
 
Lando Norris
max keeps telling me i’m thirst trapping too… i swear i didn’t intend anything of the
sort!!! this was exclusively meant to function as a guilt trip lmaoooo
 
Magui Corceiro
Subconscious thirst trapping. It’s absolutely a thing. PLEASE examine yourself. I need a
detailed account of every latent sexual thought you’ve had within the last ten days so we
can properly investigate this situation.

 
Max reads over Lando’s shoulder with shameless dedication, trying to keep track of the
conversation despite the fact it’s currently taking place inside a four-person group chat that
Max himself is already part of.
“You’re deranged,” Lando snorts. “Both of you. I genuinely think you’re just desperate to get
rid of me, so now you’re beginning to hallucinate things. This is a perfectly innocent
picture.”
Max moves away from Lando’s general sweatiness by abandoning the machine entirely and
crossing the room toward his gym bag, throwing him a deeply unimpressed glance over his
shoulder.
“Okay,” he says, rummaging through the bag in search of his water bottle. “Imagine for a
second you just met someone. Let’s say last night, in some club here. You’re instantly very,
very attracted to him, and you think there’s a reasonable chance you could get him interested
in you too.” He straightens back up again. “Now it’s the next morning. What kind of photo
are you posting to your story to get his attention?”
Lando absent-mindedly chews on his lip, tapping back onto his own story to regard it
properly. 
Yeah. He’s beginning to understand what Magui and Max are trying to imply.
“A golf pic,” he lies.
“I don’t think you would,” Max says, twisting the bottle cap open with his teeth. “Didn’t you
literally just tell me you wouldn’t want a partner who’s into golf? What kind of signal would
that send? Posting yourself looking all preppy in your little polos and whatever.”

He shakes his head, shouldering his gym bag. “No, no, Lando. You’d post something that
showed off your best feature.”
“Oh, I’m really fucking curious to hear what you think my best feature is.”
Lando takes another sip from his water bottle as Max walks back over to him, extending a
hand so Lando can haul himself upright. Max immediately tosses him a sweater afterward to
force over his sweat-soaked gym clothes so he doesn’t walk through the gym lobby looking
like that.
“Clearly it’s your body,” Max says with a jeer, as though the answer is painfully obvious.
“Sorry if you thought it was something else.”
Lando rolls his eyes as he pulls the sweater on. “You’re overthinking this.”
“Am I?”
Max throws his towel at him with the most profoundly disgusted expression imaginable.
Lando catches it mid-air, crams it into his bag, and shoulders it before following Max toward
the exit.
“I think you met someone last night,” Max continues. “You have the air.”
“What fucking air?” Lando asks, irritation beginning to creep into his voice now.
“You know. The glow. You’ve spent most of your workout staring into complete nothingness
with that slightly feverish look in your eye.”
He turns back toward Lando, holding the door open for him. “Apart from the fact,” he adds,
“that you called me this morning sounding like you were actively recovering from a
hangover.”
“I didn’t meet anyone,” Lando deflects immediately, before any sort of idea can fully take
root inside Max’s head. “I was in a voice call with my tournament coach.”
“Yeah, but after that.”
“There was no after that,” Lando says as they wander slowly out into the entrance hall, where
the elevators connect down to street level. As he passes the empty reception desk, he grabs a
mint and deftly unwraps it with still-sweaty fingers. “I went to bed afterwards.”
“Didn’t you say you went to bed late?” Max presses the elevator button as they stop in front
of the doors.
“Yeah. I was on the call with him until two.”
Max turns toward him, eyebrows raised.
There’s a shift in his expression now – something almost dangerously perceptive, as though
several previously disconnected dots have abruptly begun assembling themselves into a

coherent image inside his head.
“Oh,” he says slowly. “So you very conveniently left that information out.”
“Didn’t think it was relevant information.”
“I specifically asked you how the call with OP went, and you said it was good, that you went
over specs and keybinds and were streaming together today.” Max crosses his arms over his
chest. “You neglected to mention you were on the phone with him until two in the morning.
What the hell did you even have to talk about for that long?”
“I guess I got curious about him,” Lando admits, pushing the mint around his mouth with his
tongue until it clicks softly against his teeth. “The whole faceless thing. You know. It
activated my sleuthy instincts.” He shrugs. “Besides, he’s extremely easy to talk to.”
Max narrows his eyes at him. There is very clearly something he wants to say in response to
that – something Lando is entirely certain will fundamentally misinterpret the situation –
when the elevator doors slide open.
Before either of them can step inside, however, two figures spill out instead: tall, lanky, with
gym bags slung over their shoulders.
The unmistakably giraffe-like frame of Oliver Bearman; and, naturally, where Ollie is,
Gabriel Bortoleto is rarely far behind.
Lando’s treacherous teammate visibly startles the second he notices him standing there –
evidently one of the few people in Lando’s life who does not have his Instagram story
notifications turned on.
The quip Gabriel had clearly been halfway through saying to Ollie seems to instantly
deadlock in his throat. He coughs awkwardly and performs perhaps the single largest evasive
sidestep in recorded human history, clearly concerned Lando might momentarily forget
himself now that there are neither cameras nor Andrea Stella nearby to protect him from his
older teammate’s righteous vengeance.
Gabriel’s voice goes taut. “Norris.”
“Bortoleto,” Lando replies in the coldest tone imaginable. “Ollie.”
“Lando,” Ollie says quickly, visibly preparing to launch himself into action in an attempt to
unfuck this catastrophically awkward situation while Max merely steps farther into the
elevator doorway to stop it from sliding shut and abandoning them all here together.
“We didn’t know you were going to be here,” Ollie adds hurriedly. “Gabi and I just came
down to train for a bit.”
“We don’t need to justify being here,” Gabriel cuts in immediately with pursed lips,
confidently selecting the conversational pathway with the single worst possible outcome.
“Last I checked, this gym doesn’t belong to him.”

Max groans quietly beneath his breath, already recognising that their swift exit has very
likely just encountered a significant obstacle.
“Yeah,” Ollie says, sounding outright horrified now. “I more meant that it’s been a week and
I’m sure none of us really want–”
“Listen here, you little shit,” Lando interrupts, taking a step toward Gabriel and unfortunately
having to crane his neck upward slightly in the process as his younger teammate merely grins
down at him. “You might’ve cost me a fucking title, but you do realise this is going to stain
your record far more than mine, right?”
“Why’s that?” Gabriel asks with truly unbelievable audacity, and Lando abruptly realises that
evidently the devil himself couldn’t personally reach him, so instead he’d dispatched this
twenty-one-year-old beanpole directly from the depths of hell to torment him specifically.
“Because heated moments of uncooperative headassery are normal in this sport,” Lando says,
resisting the overwhelming urge to jab a finger directly into Gabriel’s chest. “But completely
failing to understand the scope of your own actions, and then costing your teammate a
championship because of it? That shit is going to follow you forever.”
Gabriel’s grin falters slightly.
“Next season,” Lando continues, “you’re already going to be on thin fucking ice, because
trust me, Zak is absolutely looking at replacements already. And after that? What team’s
actually going to take you?”
Gabriel looks down at him, and Lando catches the flicker of unease in the way his jaw
tightens almost imperceptibly. Because he knows Lando is fundamentally right.
The optics of costing your experienced teammate a championship – a teammate who had
fought for it fairly and squarely all season long, only to come up short because of points
Gabriel had clutched selfishly to his chest despite them changing absolutely nothing for him
in the grand scheme of things – are not exactly easy to escape.
“It had been a pattern up until that point,” Gabriel says, and for a brief moment Lando is
genuinely confused about what angle he’s trying to take.
Gabriel looks down at him, and there’s something different in his expression now beyond the
usual irritation – something almost frustratingly earnest, as though he’s trying to force Lando
into understanding his perspective.
“My races kept being sacrificed for your championship bids. Giving me second priority on
pit stops, adjusting the stupid fucking Papaya Rules in ways where no matter what I did, I
was automatically in the wrong while you were automatically in the right.” Gabriel hunches
his shoulders slightly. “So… Fernando suggested I put my foot down.”
“Rule number one of Formula One,” Lando says, biting down hard on the mint until cold
menthol floods across his tongue, “is to never take Fernando Alonso’s advice. Even if he’s
your manager.”

“It was solid advice,” Gabriel insists immediately. “I couldn’t have fucking known you’d lose
that much ground to Max during the final stretch of the season. How the hell was I supposed
to know?”
“It was my position,” Lando snaps. “You shouldn’t have kept it.”
“How is it my fault if strategy made a bad call?”
And instantly they are right back there again – exactly where they’d been after practically
every race since the summer break, when Lando’s lead had slowly melted away beneath Max
Verstappen’s relentless comeback.
Every single debrief had eventually circled back to it. Gabi, when push comes to shove, we
need to know you’ll help Lando. And every single time Gabriel had promised complete
cooperation.
It had never mattered.
Lando had always finished ahead of him regardless, and so Gabriel had been forced to hold
those three points hostage all the way through the final stretch of the season, seemingly
incapable of surrendering them at any point afterward.
“As teammates, we should be able to trust each other,” Lando snarls, and he feels it rising up
inside him again – everything he’s spent the past week trying desperately to suppress.
Happy thoughts. Happy thoughts.
“We’re supposed to be able to follow team calls like that without it turning into some ego
thing. Which it did for you.” His voice sharpens. “You couldn’t fucking stand being second to
me all season after coming off your F2 title acting all high and mighty, so you made a selfish
fucking call.” Lando takes another step closer. “And then you fucked my championship.”
Gabriel doesn’t move, but Lando catches the twitch of a muscle in his jaw. Ollie notices it too
and immediately steps between them.
“Lando, I really think you should leave now,” he says – almost pleadingly – and only the fact
that Lando genuinely likes Ollie prevents him from saying anything further. Instead, he
throws Gabriel one final venomous look.
He’s already said his piece anyway. And, more importantly, he’s made absolutely certain
Gabriel understands that he was wrong. Deeply wrong.
Lando can leave the battlefield now. So he does.
He strides into the elevator past Max, who finally steps out of the sensor’s light barrier and
presses the button for the ground floor. The last thing Lando sees before the doors slide shut
is Ollie placing a careful hand against Gabriel’s upper arm while Gabriel stands there with his
shoulders slightly slumped.

Max leans back against the elevator wall, arms folded across his chest. Something in the way
he looks at Lando makes it painfully obvious he doesn’t entirely agree with how that
interaction had just unfolded.
“Don’t even,” Lando mutters, dragging a hand through his hair.
“Haven’t said anything, have I?” Max replies, raising both hands in a gesture of innocent
surrender. “Your circus, your monkeys.”
Then he pulls out his phone in a very transparent attempt to remove himself from the
conversation he already knows Lando is going to insist on not having before inevitably
initiating it himself anyway.
Lando fundamentally needs confirmation that he’s handling this correctly. That he’s allowed
to remain angry a little while longer.
That he’s still permitted to mourn what should have been his if Gabriel, on that scorching
September afternoon in Monza, had not suddenly decided to reclaim some imagined sense of
control he believed had been denied to him all season long. With Fernando Alonso as a
mentor, honestly, Lando almost isn’t surprised.
“I mean, he started it,” Lando says, almost bashfully.
“Yeah,” Max replies, still typing away on his phone. “He did.” He glances up briefly. “Lando,
I’m not going to tell you to be the bigger man. It’s your life. Your championship. Your
teammate. This is fundamentally your situation.”
“But you do think it.”
The elevator stops. The doors slide open, and Max steps out first, Lando following him
through the inconspicuous hallway leading down toward the underground garage so neither
of them has to actually step out onto the busy street.
“Does it really matter what I think?” Max sighs.
But Lando immediately loops an arm around him from behind anyway, dropping his chin
onto Max’s shoulder. “It matters to me.”
Max attempts to turn his head enough to look at him properly, but it’s nearly impossible with
the way Lando is clinging to him from behind like some deeply emotionally compromised
backpack.
“You’re so fake,” Max sighs. “You just want me to confirm that you were completely right to
tear him a new one. You want me to hold your hand, stare deeply into your eyes, and tell you
you’ve never done anything wrong in your entire life.”
Lando widens his eyes dramatically, lower lip trembling theatrically. “You think I’ve done
something wrong before?”

“God,” Max groans, biting directly into the hand Lando has draped over his shoulder in order
to force him to let go. “We’re so fucking codependent. I need you to get a boyfriend. I
genuinely cannot keep doing this.”
“I don’t want a fucking boyfriend,” Lando whines as they descend the stairs into the
underground garage, trailing after Max toward his car.
“Yes, because you’ve realised you can get everything you need emotionally from me and
then the other thing from your Grindr matches.”
“So untrue,” Lando groans.
They reach Lando’s car first. He pops open the trunk and tosses his gym bag inside while
Max leans casually against the fender nearby.
“We didn’t finish our conversation about OP, by the way.”
“There’s nothing else to add,” Lando says, slamming the trunk shut with a loud thud.
“You were on the phone with him for twelve hours.”
“You know I love talking to people on the phone.”
“Yeah,” Max says, tilting his head slightly. “People you already know.”
“I know him now.”
“You don’t even know his name.”
“I do too.” Lando grins suddenly. “He told me. It took me twelve fucking hours, but he told
me.” His grin sharpens with smug satisfaction. “I’m playing him like a fucking fiddle,
Fewtrell. You have absolutely no idea.”
Max shakes his head. “You’re pulling my leg. No fucking way he told you his name.”
Lando steps closer to Max’s car and leans casually against the fender, propping one foot
against the tire.
“He did,” he says, tilting his head slightly. “But it took me almost twelve hours to drag it out
of him.”
“Did he face reveal to you?”
Lando shakes his head. “Unfortunately not. But I’m so on it.”
Max looks impressed despite himself, unsuccessfully attempting to flatten the corners of his
mouth in a way that still very much betrays genuine surprise – and, annoyingly enough,
respect.

“Not bad, Norris,” he admits. “I knew that kid was too much of your fanboy to resist you
forever.”
“He really tried, though,” Lando says, unable to suppress the smile tugging at his mouth at
the memory of the call; how easy Oscar had been to talk to, how strangely comfortable Lando
had felt with him almost immediately – and, in turn, the certainty that Oscar had probably felt
it too. “I think we’re actually going to become really good friends through all this.”
“I’m kind of jealous,” Max admits. “I don’t think Couriway and I are going to connect like
that. I’m clearly his second choice, and I know I’m not exactly the priority.” He snorts softly.
“Our first call lasted exactly the allotted three hours.”
“We’ll see about that,” Lando says encouragingly, twisting his wrist to glance down at his
watch. “Which reminds me – you should probably go. Your stream starts in two hours.”
Max peels himself away from Lando’s car. “You’re right.” He claps Lando once on the
shoulder, who is still leaning against the fender. “Now piss off from my car, mate.”
Lando pushes himself upright as well and turns back toward his own car, leaning briefly
against the door while he watches Max round the hood toward the driver’s side.
“Good luck, Fewtrell,” he calls after him, tilting his head slightly. “Just so you know, I
already trained clutches and OP said I’m really fucking good at them.”
Max grins at him over the roof of the car. “Oh, that’s adorable,” he calls over. “Has he figured
out your praise kink already and learned to weaponise it?”
Before Lando can protest or fire back something sarcastic, Max has already disappeared into
the driver’s seat and begun reversing out of the parking space.
Lando remains behind, rolling his eyes fondly as Max drives off. Then he pulls his phone
back out again, opens Instagram, and rewatches his own story.
Briefly, he wonders whether Max and Magui might actually have been right. Whether some
subconscious part of him had posted the picture hoping for a reaction from Oscar specifically.
But after considering the possibility for perhaps a few seconds longer than strictly necessary,
he dismisses the thought entirely.
Because, all things considered, he doesn’t exactly need pictures like that to get attention.
That’s the nice thing about being Lando Norris. He commands it anyway.


II.
 

Ten minutes before five, Lando skillfully cracks open his first can of Monster by hooking a
finger beneath the pull tab and jamming it into the condensation-slick opening just as he
clicks the Go Live button on OBS.
He leans back in his chair afterward, swivelling lazily from side to side while watching the
first messages begin trickling into chat beneath the still-static starting screen.
Then he tabs back over to Oscar’s stream.
Oscar has already been live for almost an hour, grinding ranked MCSR runs that count
toward his own championship, and ever since climbing out of the shower and throwing
together something vaguely edible before stream, Lando has found himself almost entirely
incapable of tearing away his eyes from his phone screen for more than a few seconds at a
time.
If he’d already been impressed by what Oscar was capable of before, now that he possesses
even the faintest understanding of the game itself, he’s somehow even more astonished.
Because, rationally speaking, yes, somebody who plays Minecraft eight hours a day should
presumably not be complete rubbish at it. And yet the sheer casualness with which Oscar
parkoured through a bastion while narrowly avoiding lava and piglins – all while
simultaneously reading donos and responding to chat – had still managed to leave Lando
feeling, somewhat unfortunately, deeply inadequate.
Lando had also been listening very carefully for any mention of himself.
Oscar had mentioned him eventually, though not entirely of his own volition. Chat had
started asking – through donos too, because apparently people were pathologically incapable
of minding their own business – whether he and Lando had already met up.
To which Oscar had replied, with characteristic laconic restraint, that “a set-up session had
taken place already.”
And?
And? And? And?
Chat had repeated the question a thousand different ways afterward, almost as though Lando
had somehow projected his own internal monologue directly into the stream itself.
How was it? Do you like him? Are you still a fan of him? Or does that old bonmot about
never meeting your heroes actually hold true?
At that, Oscar had taken suspiciously long to answer – a stretch of silence during which
Lando, who at that point had been unenthusiastically chewing on a piece of squeaky halloumi
he and Max had long ago nicknamed polymer cheese due to its frankly inhumane consistency,
had begun wriggling nervously around in his chair.
“He’s very nice,” Oscar had finally said, voice carefully neutral. “We hit it off well, I think.”

Chat had reacted to this with overwhelming enthusiasm, expressing – in various slightly
different iterations – their colossal relief over the fact that OP had apparently not been
entirely destroyed by exposure to the affectations of a much-too-famous professional athlete.
Lando has to admit he finds it a little charming how protective Oscar’s chat seems to be of
him. All things considered, they probably recognise some sort of kinship in him now that he’s
effectively occupying their exact position.
Chat had then immediately begun grilling Oscar about Lando’s actual aptitude for the game.
IS HE ACTUALLY WORTH HIS SALT OP???? OR DID YOU MAJORLY FUCK UP LIKE
WE TOLD YOU YOU WOULD
At that, Oscar had merely scoffed. “Guys, I know what I’m doing. I’ve followed this man’s
career for, like, ten years at this point, I think.” A pause. “He’s the only person on the current
grid I’d actually trust to pull this off.”
Then he had scoffed again. “Please stop fucking bitching and moaning about my elo lead on
Infume. I genuinely think you guys are more worried about it than I am at this point.”
Well, Lando had thought at the time, if that isn’t relatable then he genuinely doesn’t know
what is.
He, too, has to deal with approximately an entire nation of race fans catastrophising every
microscopic dip in performance. Every time he fails to qualify on the front row, he’s forced to
endure increasingly hysteria-laden questions from the British press afterward in the paddock.
It seems Oscar is dealing with much the same phenomenon. Just on a somewhat smaller
scale.
They hadn’t texted at all throughout the day. And every single time Lando had clicked back
into their Discord chat, he’d been met by the same small banner lingering stubbornly at the
bottom of the screen.
Call ended. 12 hours – Today at 3:16 a.m.
He briefly wondered what Oscar’s chat would think about the length of the call if they
actually knew about it. Lando had even considered typing something into chat himself earlier,
but with his fingers still greasy from olive oil at the time, he’d ultimately decided against it.
Mostly because he doesn’t want Oscar to feel observed by him.
Lando is almost entirely certain Oscar would instantly lose that final lingering shred of
honesty if he knew Lando was quietly lurking somewhere in his chat watching him.
And besides, Lando hadn’t wanted to divert attention away from Oscar’s genuinely absurd
sub-ten run that he’d been steadily barreling toward completing. So now he merely watches
his own chat slowly trickle in on one monitor while Oscar finishes the final run of his elo
grind on the other.

 
norris_nation223: LANDOOOOO you’re back!!!

 
Lando can’t help grinning at that. It genuinely seems as though chat hadn’t fully believed
he’d actually return – that he’d truly follow through on the promise he’d made at the end of
his previous stream.
With three minutes to spare, he finally decides to remove the starting screen and properly go
live. Before doing so, he checks himself one final time in the small OBS viewfinder.
He’d gone with a white button-down tonight, mostly because he’d cranked the heater in the
streaming room up to an almost medically irresponsible level and is already beginning to
sweat slightly; fully aware that whatever Oscar was about to attempt drilling into his brain
over the next several hours would likely require every remaining ounce of his concentration.
Which is precisely why he’s already halfway through his first Monster.

Lando attempts to forcibly school his expression back into neutrality, taking one final sip of
Monster before setting the can down beside him.
“Hey, guys,” he says, as though he hasn’t just watched chat collectively lose their minds over
a fucking shirt.
Honestly, they are incredibly easy to entertain. Though, to be fair, it is the off-season. What
else are people realistically supposed to do?
“We’re playing some Minecraft today.”
He tabs back over to Oscar’s stream again. The run is over now – Oscar having successfully
clutched the win – though the stream itself is muted, and without a facecam Lando has

Almost immediately afterward, Lando turns back toward stream. 
“And helping us in our quest to become at least marginally competent at MCSR is, of course,
my coach OP81.” He lifts the Monster can and takes another long sip. “If you weren’t here
for the first installment of this saga and are currently wondering why the hell I’m suddenly
playing Minecraft, the short version is that I’ve apparently been drafted by the current best
MCSR player alive, who is now attempting to coach me through a tournament.”
His Discord icon lights up. Lando instantly switches tabs.
“Speaking of the devil,” he says. “He’s calling me.” Then he points first toward his own eyes
and then directly into the camera. “You guys behave. I’ve summoned my old mod team back
from the dead and they are going to ban literally anybody even remotely dedicated to killing
the vibe in here.”
He’s not planning on taking any chances.
Though, admittedly, during the drafting stream he’d already discovered that his chat’s
toxicity levels remained within relatively manageable limits. Most of it consisted either of ill-
advised Max Verstappen fans who had wandered into the wrong tab or trolls attempting to
provoke some sort of reaction out of him.
The overwhelming majority of his chat usually behaves. And Lando knows they’re going to
like Oscar. Or, at the very least, be nice to him.
Then again, Oscar isn’t one of Lando’s real-life friends awkwardly guesting on stream with
absolutely no understanding of how horrific Twitch chat can occasionally become.

He’s a streamer himself. Not just casually either, but entirely immersed in that ecosystem –
somebody who has built his niche fame directly inside that sphere – meaning there is
realistically very little the internet can still surprise him with.
And judging by the almost alarmingly sharp tone Oscar occasionally uses with his own chat
whenever they start getting out of line, clearly running a fairly tight ship over there, Lando
strongly suspects he already knows exactly how to handle himself.
He slips his headphones on, adjusts the volume slightly, and finally accepts Oscar’s call.
“Hi,” Lando says, unable to stop the slightly stupid smile immediately spreading across his
face.
He never really got to say goodbye to Oscar properly yesterday considering he’d ultimately
just fallen asleep mid-call like a complete idiot, so now he finds himself disproportionately
excited to hear his voice again.
“Hi,” Oscar replies.
And Lando can’t help noticing that he sounds faintly out of breath, as though he’d just
hurried back to his desk the second Lando accepted the call. It feels strangely different
talking to him now.
Not because anything about Oscar himself has changed, but because there are suddenly
roughly twenty thousand people listening in with collective, barely concealed fascination
when yesterday evening it had simply been the two of them: Lando sitting cross-legged in
front of his oven waiting for his pizza to finish cooking. Oscar at his desk somewhere
halfway across the world, playing Minecraft while the soft clicking of his keyboard filtered
intermittently through the call.
“I told my chat you’re going to make me god-tier at Minecraft,” Lando teases as he leans
back in his chair, slowly swivelling from side to side again, only barely managing to suppress
the shit-eating grin threatening to take over his entire face.
He’s beginning to realise this might be a somewhat uneven conversation dynamic considering
Oscar can simply tab over to Lando’s stream whenever he wants and immediately see every
facial expression on his face, while Lando himself remains fundamentally barred from
discerning so much as the faintest smile ghosting across Oscar’s mouth.
Though, admittedly, after yesterday’s call he’s almost certain he can hear it in Oscar’s voice
whenever he smiles. The temperature of his drawl shifts slightly somehow; the cadence
loosens, softens, flows differently.
So at least he has that.
“Oh yeah?” Oscar says through Lando’s headphones, and Lando knows almost instinctively
that he’s smiling now. “You seem to think very highly of my coaching abilities.”

“Mainly I’m just incredibly cocksure of myself,” Lando informs him, pressing a finger
briefly against his mouth as he props his chin against his arm in a largely unsuccessful
attempt to conceal the grin tugging at the corner of his lips. “Like, pathologically convinced
I’m capable of doing anything I decide to do.”
“Evidently,” Oscar replies dryly, sounding entirely unimpressed. “Well, I’ll have you know
you’re going to die a lot today. You’re going to crash and burn and fall to your death and
drown and get blasted off cliffs and whatever else.” A pause. “Hope you’re prepared for a
little ego death. Or does your self-esteem immediately shrivel up and die the second you’re
bad at something?”
Oh. So that’s the angle Oscar is taking.
The tone he’s striking now is noticeably more teasing than it had been during their private
call yesterday – though maybe Oscar is simply beginning to relax around him now that
Lando has successfully proven himself to be, at worst, incredibly approachable and, at best,
maybe even genuinely easy to talk to.
“Oh, no need to worry,” Lando informs him easily. “My ego’s survived significantly worse
lately. I can handle a little videogame death.”
Chat absolutely loses its mind.
It somersaults, pirouettes, merges together like two motorway lanes collapsing into one
frantic stream of excitement as some of Oscar’s regular viewers begin trickling into Lando’s
chat too – grey usernames scattered throughout the otherwise brightly coloured menagerie
moving rapidly up his screen.

He has to actively suppress the deeply smug grin threatening to spread across his face when,
barely five minutes later, Oscar finally caves and loads him into a specially configured test
world built entirely around the mechanics of a perfect Zero Cycle.
Lando has already seen his fair share of One Cycle dragon fights at this point courtesy of
watching various speedruns over the past several days.
But the moment Oscar actually begins walking him through a Zero Cycle properly, Lando is
forced to immediately admit that chat – and Oscar himself – may very well have been
completely right about this.
There is absolutely no universe in which Lando is successfully pulling this off anytime soon.
He watches Oscar with something bordering on rapt attention, shutting up entirely for once as
Oscar calmly guides him through each individual step: 
Entering the End. Locating the correct position. Pillaring upward to the precise height
necessary. 
Then – and that’s the part that genuinely leaves Lando dumbstruck – the dragon actually flies
toward him, and Oscar detonates four beds in impossibly rapid succession directly against the
dragon’s hitbox, instantly draining the entire health bar to zero before pearling smoothly back
down toward the fountain platform to wait for the death animation to properly register and
finally end the game.
They watch the screen fade to black the second the portal back to the Overworld opens, and
Lando can’t help sinking his teeth briefly into his lower lip.
“That was hot,” he says immediately, leaning back in his chair again with the nearly empty
Monster can dangling loosely from one hand while an incredulous grin spreads helplessly
across his face.
God, he wants to do that. Especially now that half his chat seems fully convinced he’s never
going to successfully pull it off.
The way Oscar plays this game genuinely borders on something almost ephemeral;
something strangely beautiful to watch.
It reminds Lando, faintly, of the feeling he gets watching somebody thread a Formula One car
flawlessly through an impossibly tight chicane without deviating from the racing line even
once.
The way Max Verstappen drives, most of the time. Except this feels different somehow.
Because watching Verstappen race usually leaves behind that familiar heavy knot of
inadequacy lodged somewhere deep inside Lando’s ribs – that awful awareness of witnessing
somebody operating on a level he himself may never quite reach.
But watching Oscar play doesn’t inspire that feeling in him at all. Quite the opposite. Seeing
how good Oscar is fills him with something far closer to reverence. To pride.

As though every movement of Oscar’s hands across the keyboard, every tiny shift of his
mouse, only sharpens Lando’s own excitement instead of diminishing it.
“It’s just a Zero Cycle,” Oscar says after a moment, sounding faintly embarrassed. And
somehow – despite having absolutely no visual reference whatsoever – Lando abruptly finds
himself imagining Oscar slightly flushed.
“Sure, it’s difficult,” Oscar continues, “but most top players can do it without much–”
“Teach me,” Lando interrupts immediately, leaning forward again with the Monster can still
clutched in his hand. “Teach me how to do that in the Midoffs and I’ll dedicate my next F1
win to you. I’m being so serious right now.”
“Why?” Oscar asks after a moment. And Lando is almost certain his voice sounds slightly
hoarse now. “There’s genuinely no reason for you to learn it. If anything, it’ll just eat into
training time you very badly need.” A pause. “You’ll learn how to One Cycle. That’ll be
enough.”
“But I want to Zero Cycle.”
“No,” Oscar says firmly. “It would be a complete waste of time.”
Then, with the faint click of a command echoing softly through the call, he kicks Lando
straight back out of the test world and into the training server again, where he immediately
finds himself staring directly at the now deeply accursed facade of the desert temple.
“But–”
“Next up,” Oscar says, deliberately raising his voice just enough to bulldoze directly over
Lando’s protest, “Nether portals without flint and steel.” A brief pause. “Let’s see how you
handle that, first.”


III.
 
Within Lando’s already deeply depressing repertoire of struggle meals, steamed broccoli
occupies the absolute lowest rank imaginable.
He isn’t particularly fond of overly intense flavours at the best of times, but even he has to
admit that steamed broccoli, plain rice, and chicken with little more than a squeeze of lemon
juice barely qualifies as an actual meal and instead feels far closer to nutritional maintenance
barely masquerading as dinner.
He assembles the whole thing in the kitchen before carrying it back toward his streaming
room, depositing the plate beside his keyboard and mechanically chewing through bites of it
while the overwhelming majority of his attention remains fixed on his monitor instead.

Oscar is streaming again. 
Currently, he’s coaching Lily – the Minecraft streamer primarily famous for being part of a
large family-friendly roleplay SMP populated by various equally family-friendly Minecraft
veterans who have collectively orbited the game for what feels like approximately several
geological eras.
Lando, meanwhile, has fallen down the deeply embarrassing rabbit hole of stalking her
socials.
She has a reasonably large Instagram and Twitter following, both platforms heavily populated
with cosplay content – the latest post featuring her dressed as League of Legends’ Jinx, bright
blue wig framing her slender heart-shaped face and enormous eyes.
The comments beneath the post consist almost entirely of her friends descending into varying
degrees of mock hysteria over her beauty and absurdly accurate cosplay work, which Lily
responds to with exactly the same level of enthusiastic ardor.
Her YouTube channel is similarly massive. Every video comfortably sits somewhere above
the million-view mark, each thumbnail featuring her pink-haired Minecraft avatar plastered
across aggressively polished editing and heavily shader-modded gameplay footage.
While making dinner earlier, Lando had absentmindedly clicked through several of the
videos: a menagerie of high-end videography, fast-paced editing and cleverf comedic timing.
An aesthetic polished almost to excess, but never in a way that loses its sense of irony.
Lilyzzz – as she calls herself online – possesses a very fine, almost understated sense of
humour that Lando had immediately interpreted as evidence of considerable intelligence.
And he can already see traces of that same intelligence reflected in the way she interacts with
Oscar.
They apparently don’t know each other particularly well either. At one point she mentions
that they only properly met this morning to go over specs and settings together. Still, they
already seem to get along surprisingly well.
Lily uses a facecam, framed within an aggressively cute streaming setup complete with nerd
memorabilia carefully arranged across the massive IKEA shelves behind her – swords,
shields, banners, various collector’s editions stacked together with obvious affection.
She’s barely wearing any makeup. And honestly, she doesn’t need to. 
Even while fully concentrating – teeth sunk lightly into her lower lip as she carefully
constructs a Nether portal from a lava pool – she looks almost strangely ethereal on camera.
Oscar’s chat appears to very much agree.
 

alisaaa_1: SHE’S SO BEAUTIFUL OH MY GOD but uh, isn’t this the girl whose
Frieren cosplay went viral last year???

opberg: you should genuinely watch cornerstone smp sometime, her content is SO good
opberg: i got really hyped when op chose her as his second pick

 
Lando absently chews through another aggressively flavourless piece of broccoli while
scrolling farther down through Lily’s Instagram – and eventually he finds the cosplay in
question.
He hasn’t actually watched the anime himself, but even he vaguely remembers seeing photos
of Lily in that costume circulating online last year. And, objectively speaking, he has to admit
it really is an incredibly good cosplay.
The thought reminds him of something else entirely: he hasn’t actually checked whether
Oscar has Instagram.
Lando had simply assumed he probably wouldn’t – considering faceless streamers generally
have very little practical use for an image-focused social media platform – but he’s
immediately proven wrong the second Oscar’s profile picture appears in the search results.
There aren’t many photos. Mostly merch announcements, and a handful of tournament
graphics.
As well as one picture of his desk setup after upgrading to a PC powerful enough to probably
simulate several small alternate realities simultaneously.
While Lily’s soft voice – intermittently threaded through with Oscar’s patient explanations
and amused encouragement – filters steadily through Lando’s headphones, he finds himself
studying every visible detail of Oscar’s setup photo instead.
It’s just a desk, and obviously Oscar has gone out of his way to remove every remotely
personal detail from the image.
But still, Lando catches himself zooming in anyway, trying to determine where exactly the
light source in the room must be positioned from the angle of the shadows alone, as though
that might somehow offer him the tiniest possible glimpse into the rest of Oscar’s world.
Here too, the Follow Back button still gleams beneath Oscar’s profile picture. Lando taps it
almost automatically.
Out of instinct more than anything else, he checks the DMs there as well, though this time he
isn’t met with any strangely heartfelt late-night messages. Instead, there are only a handful of
long-expired story mentions where Oscar had apparently tagged him at various points over
the years.
Probably while watching Formula One, or maybe during the Melbourne race weekend.
Unfortunately, Instagram stories vanish after twenty-four hours, meaning Lando now has
absolutely no way of knowing. 

Slightly disappointed by this, he eventually locks his phone again and redirects his attention
back toward Oscar’s stream instead.
Lando had actually spent most of the afternoon out in the city centre with Magui and Pietra,
unsuccessfully attempting to get some Christmas shopping done for their families. And the
second he’d finally returned home to his dark apartment earlier that evening, Twitch had
immediately notified him that Oscar had gone live.
Even though they technically were not supposed to meet again until tomorrow – meaning
tonight was, in theory, Lando’s one Minecraft-free evening – he still hadn’t been capable of
not clicking on the stream anyway.
At the beginning of it, Oscar had briefly recapped their nearly four-hour training session from
the previous night, during which they had, embarrassingly enough, failed to even make it into
the Nether once and instead spent the overwhelming majority of the stream drilling various
openings ad nauseam until Lando eventually managed to complete a shipwreck route in
under three minutes.
They had both ended stream shortly afterward, and Lando had immediately gone to bed,
finally catching up on the sleep he’d lost the previous night. It had probably been for the best
because, as much as he would’ve liked to keep talking to Oscar off-stream afterward, he’d
barely been coherent by the end of the session anyway.
The exhaustion, combined with the sheer mental strain of trying to focus on the game for
hours straight, had eventually begun slurring his words together.
Now, though, he watches Lily speed effortlessly through seed after seed, and a feeling settles
heavily somewhere inside him that he is unfortunately deeply familiar with already:
Inadequacy.
That unpleasant sensation of watching somebody perform something with near effortless
precision while he himself still struggles clumsily through the basics.
But it feels different from watching Oscar play. Watching Oscar parkour flawlessly through
bastions, build portals within seconds, or locate buried treasure with terrifying efficiency
doesn’t really bother Lando in quite the same way because Oscar is his coach.
Oscar being ruthlessly talented at something only feels like an extension of Lando’s own
advantage considering he’s the one being trained by him.
Lily, however, is direct competition.
And even though she technically occupies a different side of the bracket – because two
mentees coached by the same speedrunner are unable to face each other early on – Lando
instinctively knows that, in their current states, she would absolutely wipe the floor with him.
Which honestly feels a little unfair – because technically speaking she does play Minecraft
professionally too. Admittedly a completely different version of Minecraft – non-

competitive, heavily edited, roleplay-heavy Minecraft – but still fundamentally the same
game nonetheless.
She already knows things Lando had to discover through painful humiliation yesterday; like
the fact that lava poured onto water creates obsidian while the reverse merely produces
completely useless cobblestone.
Of course she’s better. Even though she’s only Oscar’s second pick.

Lando carries his empty plate back toward the kitchen and loads it into the dishwasher before
turning the machine on despite it currently containing little beyond several coffee mugs and
one aggressively depressing dinner plate.
Then he rummages distractedly through the fridge in search of literally anything more
interesting to drink than yet another Monster. Finding absolutely nothing, he ultimately
settles for a second can anyway before wandering back toward his desk.
In the meantime, Lily and Oscar have drifted naturally into a conversation about their
respective careers within Minecraft content creation. Lando settles back into his chair cross-
legged, absentmindedly brushing his thumb across the rough aluminium surface of the can
while quietly listening in.
Lily has a soft English accent perfectly suited to her entire demeanour, and it forms an
unexpectedly pleasant contrast against Oscar’s lower register and loose Australian drawl.
She laughs often at his jokes, and Lando finds himself staring at her facecam longer than
strictly necessary while sipping from his Monster and listening to them talk.
He feels, strangely, a little as though he’s intruding somehow. As though they are currently
discovering in real time that they genuinely get along remarkably well, and their quiet delight
over that discovery seems entirely untouchable by the fact that roughly fifteen thousand
people – Lando included – are currently listening in.
Though, of course, they don’t actually know he’s there.
“That’s what I love about this game,” Lily says at one point while effortlessly swimming
through the tiny shipwreck opening and looting the chest within mere seconds, as though
she’s repeated the exact movement a thousand times before – which, realistically speaking,
she probably has. Just in an entirely different context.
“There are just so many different directions you can take it. Like, you got into speedrunning
while I ended up focusing on building and RPG content and stuff.” She laughs softly. “But
it’s still all technically the same game.”
“Yeah,” Oscar replies. “Though while you’re obviously not rubbish at Minecraft
speedrunning, I genuinely don’t think you could ever teach me how to pick a colour palette or

build literally anything more complicated than a dirt hut.”
Lily laughs again. It’s a warm sound, almost windchime-like. Lando finds himself
unexpectedly entranced by it.
“Oh, OP,” she says, still laughing slightly, “when all this is over, you absolutely have to visit
the Cornerstone SMP sometime. I’d love to show you around.”
“Deal,” Oscar replies.
Lando immediately takes an enormous sip from his Monster because he’s almost certain he
can hear Oscar smiling again through the slight shift in his voice. And briefly, despite
himself, he wonders whether Lily hears it too.
Whether she has already spent enough time talking to Oscar to begin recognising the tiny
changes in timbre and cadence the same way Lando has. Whether she has already started
translating them into moods too.
They start to nerd out quite quickly after that, speaking about their favourite anime and
games besides Minecraft – both realising almost in real time that they are, in fact, equally
obsessed with Genshin Impact. Lily even briefly stops her training to show Oscar some
pictures of new cosplay concepts she’s planning to wear to VidCon in the spring of next year.
Lando keeps sitting there cross-legged on his chair, fiddling with his phone, absent-mindedly
scrolling through Instagram while he listens to a conversation in which he should,
realistically speaking, have absolutely no emotional stake whatsoever.
He should text Magui, ask her if she wants to go out tonight – it’s been a while since he’s
gotten properly drunk in a Monaco club again, and one and a half weeks of mourning period
regarding his lost championship honestly seem sufficient enough for him; after that he’s
probably allowed to start having fun again. 
But instead he just sits there in his dark room in front of his PC, watching somebody stream a
Minecraft speedrunning practice, which is, frankly, deeply unbecoming of him and the sort of
person he’s spent years turning himself into. 
Lando’s got a reputation of being something close to a wildfire, of barely staying home
voluntarily at all, perpetually ricocheting between people and noise and movement. After all,
he’s got an entire chain of people he calls the second he’s forced to hear his own thoughts for
longer than a few uninterrupted minutes.
But Max is out with Pietra tonight, and if Lando texts Magui then they’ll inevitably end up
drunk together in some overcrowded club until four in the morning like they always do; and
the more Lando turns that possibility around in his head, the less he actually wants it.
In fact, there’s really only one thing he wants. He wants to spend more time with his coach –
off-stream.

In some strange way, their last actual conversation, which admittedly had been exorbitant in
length, already feels oddly distant despite the fact that it has only been two days; and since
then every interaction between them has unfolded publicly in front of thousands of viewers
while Lando repeatedly humiliates himself at the game for everyone’s collective
entertainment.
He opens Discord, briefly considering shooting Oscar a message – but what is he even
supposed to say? Something along the lines of: Hey, do you maybe want to accidentally
spend another twelve hours on call together? There are still things I need to find out about
you.
No, obviously not. Oscar would probably think he’d completely lost his mind. 
So Lando closes Discord again and instead watches Oscar’s chat coo over Lily and Oscar’s
warm conversation and the almost alarming natural talent she seems to possess for the game. 
Slowly, almost visibly, Oscar’s community begins allowing itself to hope again: maybe
Oscar’s not entirely fucked after all; maybe, even if unreflected fanboyism apparently forced
his hand when it came to picking Lando, Lily might still end up coming in clutch hard
enough to drag him past the first day of the tournament.
Briefly, he considers typing something in chat just to draw attention to himself, simply
because he knows chat would absolutely lose its collective mind over it, that screenshots of
his message would be on Twitter within seconds and around two thousand additional viewers
would probably come flooding into the stream immediately afterward. 
There’s a part of him which is endlessly curious about how Oscar would react if he knew
Lando had been lurking there since the starting screen, had listened to him joke around with
chat and talk to Lily while Lando himself stood in his kitchen steaming broccoli and chicken
like the most profoundly pathetic twenty-something bachelor imaginable.
By now, Lily and Oscar have more or less abandoned training entirely – all in all, they only
properly focused for around two hours as opposed to the four Oscar had dragged Lando
through yesterday – and instead have fully dissolved into exchanging increasingly niche
anime and videogame recommendations while chat occasionally interjects here and there
with suggestions of their own.
Lando pulls his phone back out of his pocket, swiping instinctively toward Discord before
clicking on Oscar’s profile.
Whatever. He’s just going to do it. There’s genuinely no reason to be this self-conscious
about the entire thing; Oscar would not have spent almost twelve uninterrupted hours on call
with him if he hadn’t, to some extent, enjoyed talking to him too – so there’s probably no real
harm in suggesting an encore.
