Maybe he shouldn’t be telling Oscar things like that, Lando slowly begins to realise. Maybe
he should calm down a little and simply wait until Oscar actually gets off stream, especially
considering he’s very obviously ignoring him on purpose right now.
Or maybe – and this only occurs to Lando after a certain amount of time has passed without
any reply whatsoever – Oscar is, in fact, very deliberately proving a point.
Lando begins chewing on the inside of his lip at that realisation, absent-mindedly tapping
against his display before it can dim and shut off from inactivity, while on Twitch Oscar
finally wraps up stream, sending his viewers off in a raid toward Feinberg’s channel with the
casual efficiency of someone who has performed this exact routine a thousand times before.
And then, not even five seconds later, Lando’s phone vibrates directly in his hand.
Oscar is calling him.
He watches the Discord caller ID flash up across his display and, for a moment, simply lets it
ring there in front of him, like he wants to savour the fact that Oscar is actually calling him
before he finally accepts the call, holding the phone close to his face as he slowly swivels
around in his chair.
“Hi,” he says after a moment, unable to properly suppress the bright grin threatening to split
his face in two.
“Hi,” Oscar replies, and instantly Lando thinks his voice sounds different than it did on
stream somehow – a little breathless again, maybe, and not quite as low and drawling as it
becomes whenever he deadpans his way through donations and chat messages in front of an
audience.
“You took your sweet time,” Lando says, still grinning as he catches his thumbnail between
his teeth and pulls one leg up onto the chair so he can prop his phone against his knee.
“Oh, you think you can call and I just come running?” There’s a thread of self-irony woven
through Oscar’s voice considering that this is, more or less, exactly what just happened.

“How was your stream?” Lando asks instead, despite the fact that he’d literally been there for
the entire thing.
“Good,” Oscar says. “A little draining.”
“Why?”
“It’s hard for me to talk to people I don’t know very well,” Oscar admits after a moment,
sounding faintly embarrassed by the concession and yet apparently still willing to make it
anyway, as though honesty between them has already become some sort of solemnly
established expectation. “And I don’t know Lily very well.”
And yet he had spent nearly twelve uninterrupted hours on call with Lando seemingly
without struggling to speak to him at all. Lando notices the discrepancy immediately, but
doesn’t point it out.
“Do you prefer streaming alone, then?” Lando asks, nudging his mouse absent-mindedly
across the trackpad so that his monitor – now automatically playing Feinberg’s stream after
Oscar raided him – doesn’t dim and shut itself off.
“I do like streaming with my friends,” Oscar says, and Lando is almost certain he hears him
stand up because suddenly there’s a strange series of violent cracking sounds echoing through
the call.
“What the hell was that?”
“You heard that?” Oscar sounds genuinely embarrassed now.
“Yeah,” Lando laughs. “It sounded like someone snapping glowsticks in half.”
“That’s just my back,” Oscar scoffs. “My body violently punishes me whenever I forget to
move for several hours straight, but unfortunately my brain regularly forgets I even
physically exist.”
Lando laughs harder at that, dropping his head briefly against the backrest of his chair.
“Should’ve become an athlete, then.”
“I played cricket in school,” Oscar says after a moment, and instantly Lando’s imagination
betrays him again, reconstructing Oscar in front of that desk from the Instagram picture,
stretching his arms above his head while every joint in his body cracks violently into place.
In Lando’s mind, his shirt rides up slightly in the process, exposing a narrow strip of pale
skin across his stomach.
Which almost annoys him a little. 
Apparently his imagination is perfectly capable of inventing exposed skin and body language
and posture, but still fundamentally refuses to provide him with a face to attach any of it to.
“God,” Lando says, grinning as he pushes himself out of his chair, “you’re so Australian.”

And, unfortunately, he likes that immensely. He’s always had a soft spot for Australia – not
least because of his former teammate who left the sport last year entirely on his own terms –
but also because he’s always liked going there in general; the accents, the strange words they
insist on using for painfully ordinary objects, the almost aggressive friendliness of the people.
“Guilty as charged,” Oscar scoffs, and Lando crosses the room before throwing himself
dramatically onto the couch on the opposite side of his office, the one usually reserved for
discarded hoodies and miscellaneous streaming equipment whenever he’s live.
Lando lets his phone rest against the middle of his chest, which causes it to vibrate faintly
every time Oscar’s voice comes through the speakers.
“Be honest,” he says. “Are you wearing a cricket shirt right now?”
There’s a pause on the other end of the call. Then, sounding a little embarrassed: “Are you
somehow actually able to see me?”
Lando laughs immediately, genuinely delighted by that reaction. “No,” he says. “I just
figured you were exactly the kind of guy whose entire wardrobe consists exclusively of
sports shirts.”
“Yeah,” Oscar admits after a moment. “Unfortunately you’re right about that.” A pause. “I
used to stick out like a sore thumb at uni because most of my–”
Oscar cuts himself off so abruptly that Lando immediately sits upright, the phone sliding off
his chest and dropping beside him onto the couch cushions.
“Did you just–” Lando stops himself halfway through the sentence before grinning suddenly.
“Oscar, did you just accidentally let something slip?”
“What?” Oscar says quickly, sounding faintly mortified now. “You already knew I went to
uni.”
“Yeah,” Lando says, sitting up fully now, “but now I’m suddenly extremely convinced you
studied either something horrifically preppy or something super nerdy.”
“You’re jumping to conclusions.” Oscar is good at keeping his voice carefully level whenever
he wants to, but Lando is still completely convinced he’s onto something now.
“I’m pretty sure you didn’t study something preppy,” Lando continues, already pacing around
the room now because apparently his body has decided today still didn’t contain enough
movement despite spending half the afternoon Christmas shopping with Magui and Pietra.
“So I’m assuming you studied something deeply nerdy where everybody wore giant washed-
out hoodies with, like, obscure maths jokes on them.”
“What exactly makes you think I couldn’t have studied something preppy?” Oscar asks
immediately, sounding almost oddly intent on hearing whatever version of him Lando has
apparently assembled inside his own head. “I absolutely could have.”

“Yeah, sure,” Lando scoffs. “You were definitely on track to become a lawyer. That’s why
you spend eight hours a day speedrunning Minecraft.”
“I am not disclosing anything,” Oscar replies, sounding mildly offended now. “Though I do
feel slightly insulted by the fact that you apparently believe I’d be incapable of studying law.”
Lando snickers. “I genuinely don’t know how to explain this to you, Oscar, but there is
absolutely no universe in which you didn’t study something unbelievably nerdy.”
A pause.
“Something unbelievably nerdy?”
“You know,” Lando says smugly, “the only way to prove me wrong is by telling me.”
Oscar goes quiet for a moment. Then, finally: “I see you still haven’t given up.”
“Trying to figure out who you are?” Lando immediately doubles back across the room the
second he reaches the opposite wall, throwing himself onto the couch again with enough
force to make the cushions wheeze underneath him. “I told you already. I’m not letting that
go.”
“Did you lure me into this call under false pretenses?” Oscar asks dryly. “Was that the urgent
question you wanted to ask me?”
“No,” Lando says quickly, scrambling a little the second he realises there genuinely hadn’t
actually been a question in the first place – he’d simply wanted to talk to him again. “I, uh–”
He clears his throat. “I wanted to ask whether you’d teach me how to Zero Cycle.”
Oscar groans instantly. “Lando.”
God, he really likes the way Oscar says his name like that. There’s already something weirdly
familiar about it now, something that makes it sound as though they’ve known each other
properly for ages instead of barely forty-eight hours.
“Why do you refuse to teach me?” Lando complains, sprawling farther across the couch
dramatically.
“Because I genuinely do not think we should be investing our time into that,” Oscar says.
“We have three hours every two days for two weeks, during which you somehow need to
learn how to play the entirety of Minecraft speedrunning at a level that ideally results in a
sub-thirty finish. I’m not sinking countless hours into teaching you an extremely advanced
mechanic that saves maybe three minutes maximum in an actual run. The ratio there is
catastrophic.”
Lando sulks immediately, throwing one arm over his eyes. “And what if you teach me off-
stream?”
There’s another small pause from the other side of the call before Oscar clears his throat
faintly. “Uh. Off-stream?”

“Yeah,” Lando says, rolling his eyes despite the fact that Oscar obviously cannot see it. “You
know. Not on stream.” A beat. “Like right now.”
“Right now?” Lando can practically hear Oscar’s eyebrows climbing upward. “Don’t you
have literally anything better to do?”
“I very much do not,” Lando snorts. “Max is out with his girlfriend, and if I call my own
girlfriend she’s just going to drag me into getting catastrophically drunk somewhere, and
honestly I really, really want to learn how to Zero Cycle without your terrifyingly
judgemental audience criticising every single thing I do.”
Yet again, Oscar goes quiet for a little too long, and Lando briefly finds himself wondering
what exactly he does during those pauses – whether he’s pacing around his room, whether
he’s stretching again, whether he’s staring at his monitor while thinking about what to say.
“If you genuinely have nothing else to do,” Oscar finally says, “then I’d love to teach you.”
Lando immediately pumps his fist into the air triumphantly. “Fuck yeah, Osc.”
Another pause. Then, sounding slightly hoarse: “Osc?”
“Don’t tell me you’re secretly one of those deeply boring people who hate nicknames,”
Lando says as he pushes himself off the couch and crosses back toward his desk, closing
Twitch before reopening Minecraft, which has remained sitting untouched on his PC ever
since he ended stream yesterday evening. He switches Discord over onto his headset too
before pulling it properly over his ears.
“I’m not,” Oscar says. “I’m just a little… unfamiliar with them, I guess.”
“What do you mean?” Lando asks. “Nobody’s ever given you a nickname before?”
“Uh, my family doesn’t really do nicknames,” Oscar says after a moment. “And most of my
friends just call me OP, which I suppose technically already is a nickname in itself.”
“It doesn’t count if you basically gave it to yourself,” Lando says as the Minecraft launcher
loading bar flashes rapidly across his screen. He leans back farther in his chair, squeezing his
stress toy absent-mindedly in one hand while he waits for the game to finish booting up.
“And it counts even less when your nickname is just openly complimentary. Like OP. Like
overpowered. That’s not a nickname, you’re just flexing.”
“Hm,” Oscar hums. “I think I just wasn’t particularly creative when I came up with my
Minecraft username at, like, ten.”
“No, it’s nice,” Lando says immediately. “And the eighty-one is weirdly reminiscent of a
driver number too. Like I’ve got the four.”
Oscar helps him install the Zero Cycle practice mod, and under Lando’s relentless begging he
demonstrates the entire thing one more time from the beginning. It barely takes him thirty
seconds altogether.

“You’re so good at this,” Lando says, genuinely winding the cable of his headphones around
his finger while he watches Oscar move through the setup with terrifying ease. “Like, I think
I could literally watch this forever.”
“Well,” Oscar replies dryly, “you’re going to be really, really bad at it considering you still
fundamentally do not know how to two-plus-two.”
“I know it’s four.”
A deep sigh echoes through the call. “That’s not what that… whatever. You’re such a fucking
clown.”
Still: Oscar genuinely might be the greatest teacher Lando has ever encountered in his life, he
becomes increasingly convinced of that the longer their impromptu private lesson stretches
on. 
There’s something almost unsettling about the way Oscar seems to instinctively understand
how Lando’s brain works, anticipating every snag before he even fully crashes into it,
heading off frustrations before they can properly form, explaining things in three different
ways if necessary and never once sounding annoyed by the fact that Lando keeps asking
questions every thirty seconds. 
He’d already been patient with him on stream, of course, never mocking him properly, never
genuinely losing his temper despite the fact that Lando had, objectively speaking, behaved
like an absolute nightmare student for most of it – but here, off-stream, without an audience
watching them, Lando gets the strange impression that Oscar genuinely loves teaching, loves
the process of figuring people out intellectually, loves questions almost as much as he loves
answering them.
It doesn’t actually help very much, unfortunately.
Lando is absolutely catastrophic at Zero Cycling, which admittedly should not come as much
of a surprise considering he has still never even killed the dragon normally before and has
instead immediately insisted on attempting the single hardest possible variation of the fight.
But Lando, too, can become frighteningly patient the second he genuinely wants something
badly enough.
And oh, he wants this.
Lando is deeply surprised by two things: firstly, by the fact that he manages to stay focused
on something for almost four uninterrupted hours without drifting off even once – not even
when Magui texts him asking whether he wants to come over, watch a movie and help her
drink some leftover Limoncello she apparently still has sitting around from an ill-fated art
project. He tells her he’s busy playing Minecraft, to which she replies with a single deeply
judgemental: BOOOOO!!!
The second thing surprising him, however, is Oscar himself.

More specifically the fact that Oscar does not, at any point throughout the evening, seem to
grow visibly tired of him.
Because realistically speaking, this has got to be the most excruciating four hours of Oscar’s
entire recent existence. Lando is progressing at an almost glacial pace, repeatedly fumbling
inputs, panicking under pressure, misplacing blocks and accidentally detonating himself in
increasingly creative ways – and yet Oscar never once tries to end the call early, never begins
lapsing into terse monosyllabic replies, never even remotely sounds like he’s attempting to
escape the conversation. 
If anything, the longer the evening stretches on, the softer that faintly sarcastic but
undeniably indulgent edge in his voice becomes whenever he talks to Lando, as though
somewhere along the line he has stopped treating this like a coaching obligation and started
genuinely enjoying himself instead.
And at some point, as it grows late again without either of them properly noticing, the
conversation slowly slips away from Minecraft altogether and back into more personal
territory – Oscar suddenly beginning to ask Lando questions about practically everything
under the sun while continuing to respond with extraordinarily skilled evasions and dry
sarcasm whenever Lando attempts to pry anything substantial out of him in return.
“Don’t think I don’t know what you’re doing,” Lando says at some point, chewing absent-
mindedly on the string of his hoodie while sprawled across the couch in his living room,
watching the shadows from the street outside drift slowly across the ceiling of his apartment. 
His voice has gone slightly sleepy around the edges by now, words beginning to soften and
blur together a little, and he thinks Oscar’s beginning to slur faintly too despite the fact that,
technically speaking, it’s the middle of the day for him.
He genuinely had not been lying when he said his sleeping schedule was fucked.
“What am I doing?” Oscar asks after a moment.
“You’re trying to gather compromising material on me,” Lando replies, grinning. “So you can
eventually blackmail me into getting you paddock passes or whatever.”
Oscar laughs quietly at that, and it’s such a soft sound that Lando immediately smiles too,
something indulgent and warm threaded through it, perfectly matching the tone their entire
conversation has settled into over the past hours – a constant back and forth where they keep
swinging rubber weapons at each other, carefully aiming only for places where they know the
other person will not mind.
“Sure,” Oscar says, and Lando can hear the smile in his voice immediately. He sounds like he
smiles with dimples, Lando decides suddenly, with the strange certainty of somebody
inventing details about a face he still fundamentally cannot picture properly. “That’s exactly
what I’m doing.”
“Genuinely, though,” Lando says after a moment, his tone softening slightly as he stares up
toward the ceiling again. “I’d actually love to send you a paddock pass for Melbourne

sometime.” A beat. “I’d love to meet you.”
Silence.
Not the easy kind they’ve settled into naturally over the course of the evening either, not the
comfortable pauses where one of them stretches or resets the game or gets water – this one
lands heavier somehow, suddenly dragging something up to the surface that Oscar very
clearly had not wanted there.
“I don’t know,” Oscar says eventually, after long enough that Lando has already sat upright
again, chewing on the edge of his thumbnail while staring at the phone balanced against his
knee like it might somehow reveal the expression currently crossing Oscar’s face. His voice
sounds guarded now. Careful. As though he’s trying very hard not to say too much and
accidentally expose something underneath it.
“Why not?” Lando asks immediately. “I’m sure we’d have fun together.”
“I think it’d be too risky,” Oscar says, and the words sound almost physically reluctant
leaving him. “There’s a reason for the whole faceless thing. I don’t exactly love the idea of
people connecting–”
“They won’t,” Lando interrupts him quickly. “You wouldn’t have to be in the garage where
all the cameras are. We’ve got private areas too.” He grins slightly. “Loads of drivers keep
their secret girlfriends there.”
Or hookups and casual flings they want to impress without attracting headlines, Lando adds
mentally, considering he himself has done precisely that often enough while Magui loyally
holds position in the garage acting as his social camouflage.
“I’ll think about it,” Oscar says after a moment. “Though I promise I am not collecting
information to blackmail you eventually. I’m just… curious.”
“In the person behind the mask?” Lando jokes lightly.
But Oscar doesn’t laugh this time. 
“Yeah,” he says. “Like… in a way.”
And then he stops there, clearly too embarrassed to let the conversation move any closer
toward the uncomfortable truth lingering underneath all of this – namely the fact that Oscar’s
digital footprint still suggests years and years of fandom toward him, something he
consistently seems unwilling to acknowledge aloud for longer than absolutely necessary.
Lando feels himself swallow around that. “I’m mostly the same,” he concedes. Emphasis on
mostly.
“You are,” Oscar replies immediately, and his voice has softened again in that particular way
that makes Lando think he must be smiling.

Lando finds himself wondering what exactly he’s doing right now. Whether he’s lying on his
bed as well, considering there’s been the faint rustle of fabric through the call every now and
then for the last several minutes. Whether the sun, which abandoned Monaco hours ago
already, is currently spilling lazily across Oscar’s room instead, drawing warmth from his
hair and skin in hues of gold. Whether he really is still wearing some ancient cricket jersey
like he’d accidentally revealed earlier, meaning the entire image in Lando’s head is washed in
faded greens and yellows.
He wonders what Oscar would look like in orange.
“Give me your address,” Lando says suddenly, and Oscar laughs instantly.
“No,” he says. “Absolutely not.”
“Fine,” Lando groans dramatically, momentarily forgetting the extent of Oscar’s caginess
regarding literally anything remotely personal. “Then give me the address of a P.O. box
you’ve got easy access to.”
“Why?”
“Because I want to send you something, dumbass.”
Oscar snorts softly. “A pipe bomb? A severed goat head? A tracking device?”
“Nothing of the sort,” Lando reassures him while already switching apps on his phone to text
Kristen from merch operations.
“Fine,” Oscar says eventually. “Purely because you’ve managed to pique my curiosity.” A
pause. “There isn’t actually a post office box anywhere particularly near me, but my sister
lives close to one of those parcel collection centres. I’ll text you the address.”
“Ha,” Lando says immediately, pouncing on the information before Oscar can retract it. “So
your sister’s old enough to live alone.”
“Yeah, Lando,” Oscar says softly, and Lando genuinely never knows anymore which details
Oscar will hand over without resistance and which ones he guards with almost absurd
carefulness. “She’s turning twenty-three in a couple of days.”
“So she’s really close to you in age then,” Lando says instantly, already doing the maths in
his head. “Like, maximum a year and a half younger.”
“Yes,” Oscar says, and he sounds impossibly fond suddenly, warmth bleeding through every
syllable. Immediate green flag, Lando decides. In his experience, men who genuinely adore
their sisters usually turn out the best. “She’s kind of my best friend.”
His phone vibrates lightly against his knee and, when he checks the chat, he finds that Oscar
has actually sent him an address somewhere near the centre of Melbourne. Lando
immediately copies it into Google Maps purely because he wants to look at it for a second,
absurdly pleased by the fact that he’s managed to extract yet another tiny piece of Oscar’s life
out of him.

Then he tabs back into the text he’s currently drafting for Kristen.
Hey, Kristen. Hope you’re well. Please excuse the late message and absolutely ignore
this until you’re actually working again, haha. Could you do me a massive favour and
assemble a PR merch box with Quadrant, LN4 and McLaren merch and send it to this
address in Melbourne? Thank you xx, L

He sends it without much additional thought.
“What are you scheming?” Oscar asks after a moment. “Are you currently doing something
weird?”
“Nah,” Lando grins, sinking farther down into the couch cushions again. “Don’t worry about
it.” A beat. “What did you study?”
“You are not going to blindside me by abruptly changing the topic,” Oscar snorts.
“I just know it was something deeply nerdy,” Lando yawns. “Like, I’m so confident about
this that I’d genuinely wager an irresponsible amount of money on it.”
Oscar sighs – and Lando genuinely never sees the exact moment coming where Oscar finally
gives up resisting him. He suspects Oscar probably doesn’t see it coming either.
“Yeah, fine,” he says eventually. “It was something nerdy.”
“Oh my god,” Lando says delightedly. “So you’re secretly a genius.”
“No,” Oscar says immediately, sounding embarrassed all over again.
“You are,” Lando laughs. “That is exactly what somebody says when they’re secretly a
genius but learned very early on not to mention it because people bullied them over it.”
“I’m not a genius,” Oscar insists, sounding oddly adamant about it. “I’m lazy as hell. My
mum gives me shit for it constantly. Says I could be in a completely different place in life if I
wasn’t fundamentally lacking ambition.”
“Let me guess,” Lando says. “She doesn’t exactly consider Minecraft speedrunning a viable
long-term career path.”
“No,” Oscar admits after a tiny pause. “She wants me to actually use my degree. Says it’s a
shame I put myself through all that just to let it collect dust somewhere while I sit on my ass
playing Minecraft all day.”
“I mean,” Lando teases lightly, “she’s probably worried you don’t have any friends. If you
play Minecraft eight hours a day, sleep exclusively during daylight hours, live alone and call
your sister your best friend, realistically speaking how populated can your social life actually
be?”
Oscar doesn’t answer immediately, and Lando feels bad about it almost at once.

“Sorry,” he says after a moment. “That was genuinely kind of shitty. I didn’t mean–”
“I’m not offended, dude,” Oscar interrupts him, and from his tone Lando can tell he
genuinely means that. “I’m honestly just annoyed because I’ve been trying so hard not to tell
you anything about myself, and somehow you still keep reading me to absolute filth.” A
pause. “You’re not supposed to be this observant.”
Lando laughs quietly. “I’m not supposed to be this observant?”
“Like, yeah,” Oscar says, his voice lower now somehow, softer around the edges. “You’re not
really supposed to be… any of this, actually.”
“What does that mean?”
Another pause. “Like…” Oscar exhales faintly. “Nice.” He sounds vaguely embarrassed by
the admission. “Aren’t you supposed to be, like, incredibly busy all the time?”
“I mostly just keep busy whenever I hate myself,” Lando says before he can stop himself. He
really should not be giving away this much of himself this quickly, but unfortunately he has
always been fundamentally incapable of keeping his heart properly hidden for long.
“So you don’t currently hate yourself?”
Lando laughs softly. “No. Currently I mostly just hate Gabriel Bortoleto.” A beat. “Did I tell
you I ran into him at the gym today?”
“No,” Oscar says, in the tone of somebody for whom these sorts of personal debriefs have
already become entirely normal despite the fact that this is technically only the second proper
phone call of their entire lives. “Did you beat him up?”
“Almost,” Lando groans. “But he’s annoyingly taller than me.”
“That’s not particularly difficult.”
“Fuck you,” Lando says automatically, though immediately another opening presents itself to
him and he sinks his teeth into it at once. “Wait. So you’re taller than me?”
“How tall are you again?”
“Five nine.”
“Mmh.” Oscar sounds smug suddenly, like he’s grinning to himself somewhere on the other
side of the world. “I’m five ten.”
“Wow,” Lando snorts, though he immediately files the information away carefully regardless.
“I could still beat you in a fight, I think.”
“Why exactly do you think that, Norris?”

“Because I’m an athlete,” Lando says, “and you’re fundamentally just some scrawny nerd
who sits around playing video games all day.”
Oscar laughs at that like he knows something Lando doesn’t. “Yeah,” he says. “You could
absolutely beat me in a fight.”
They lapse into silence for a little while after that, the easy sort they’ve somehow already
grown used to over the course of the evening, before Lando eventually circles back toward
something that’s been lingering in the back of his mind for the past hour.
“I found your Instagram today, by the way.”
“Hm.” Oscar sounds unimpressed. “Did you now?”
“Very disappointed by the severe lack of embarrassingly heartfelt DMs,” Lando teases. “I
was really looking forward to uncovering some more deeply concerning parasocial
behaviour.”
“You’re genuinely insufferable,” Oscar groans immediately. “Like, fundamentally unbearable
as a person.”
“You did tag me in your story a weird amount though,” Lando continues, grinning to himself.
“What was that about?”
“Wouldn’t you like to know.”
Oscar’s voice sounds heavier now somehow, sleepier around the edges, and Lando hears
more fabric rustling through the call which immediately conjures the image again, unbidden
and vivid: Oscar half-buried in his sheets somewhere on the other side of the world,
exhausted beyond belief but still stubbornly refusing to end the call.
“Oh, come on,” Lando says, pouting despite the fact that Oscar cannot see it. “It can’t have
been that bad if you posted it publicly.”
“It’s one thing to do something,” Oscar mutters, “and an entirely different thing to later admit
it directly to the person involved.”
“What was it?”
Oscar mumbles something into the phone.
“Hm? Didn’t catch that.”
A pause.
Then, clearer this time: “I said I was probably congratulating you on every single race win
you ever fucking got like an absolute loser.”
Lando grins so hard his face genuinely begins to hurt. “No fucking way, Osc,” he says
delightedly. “You are genuinely adorable.”

“I regret the day I ever became a fan of you,” Oscar mutters, though he sounds significantly
more awake now, as though the conversation has suddenly become too dangerous for him to
continue navigating while half-asleep. As though he’s realised he might accidentally let slip
things he doesn’t actually want Lando hearing.
“When did you become a fan of me?” Lando asks softly.
“Ages ago,” Oscar says. “Like… I think you were still in Formula Two. Maybe even Formula
Three.”
“Why were you even watching those categories?” Lando asks. “That’s not really something
casual fans do.”
“I’m not a casual fan,” Oscar replies dryly. “Haven’t you figured that out by now?”
And suddenly, a suspicion unfurls quietly somewhere inside Lando’s chest. He hesitates over
it for a second before finally voicing it anyway. 
“Did you…” He pauses briefly. “Did you ever want to get into the sport yourself?”
That earns him the longest silence yet. When Oscar finally speaks again, his voice sounds
noticeably tighter.
“Yeah,” he says. “Briefly.”
Something strange twists inside Lando immediately upon hearing that, something sharp and
almost painful, like suddenly being able to physically see the red thread that’s somehow been
stretching between them this entire time.
“What happened?” he asks carefully.
And when Oscar answers, his voice sounds softer than Lando has ever heard it before. 
“My mum wouldn’t let me move to England.” A pause. “My dad was completely on board.
He’d already sorted everything out.” Oscar exhales quietly. “But she told us she couldn’t let
me leave.”
Another pause.
“She took it really badly. Like… really badly. And it put an enormous strain on my family.”
His voice lowers further. “I knew something was eventually going to break if we actually
went through with it. My parents probably would’ve ended up divorced, and my sisters
would’ve gotten caught in the middle of all of it.” A small shrug seems to thread invisibly
through the sentence. “So I stepped away.”
Lando doesn’t know what to say to that.
“Fuck, Osc,” he says quietly after a moment. “I’m really sorry.”

“It’s fine,” Oscar says immediately. “I barely think about it anymore.” His voice lightens
deliberately again, almost forcibly. “I probably would’ve been rubbish anyway.”
Lando doesn’t believe that for even half a second.
“But I stayed invested in the sport,” Oscar continues. “And at some point I guess I became a
fan of you. George Russell too. Alex Albon.” A pause. “But mainly you.”
“Why me?” Lando asks softly, still feeling strangely unsure how to navigate this conversation
now. It suddenly feels unfair somehow to sit here as the person who actually got to live the
dream Oscar lost.
“Don’t know,” Oscar says after a moment. “I guess I always thought you seemed like
somebody who’d be fun to know.” He laughs quietly to himself. “And you talked about
videogames a lot, which became pretty much the main thing I got into after the racing thing
didn’t work out.”
Lando sits with that for a moment, turning the words around quietly in his head. “I’m sorry
you didn’t get to live your dream,” he says eventually.
“It’s fine,” Oscar insists immediately. “Like I said, I genuinely barely think about it
anymore.”
“You found something else to become insanely good at,” Lando says softly, dragging one of
the cushions beside him over his lap because he’s beginning to feel slightly cold now that the
apartment has settled fully into nighttime. “Like… you’re literally the best Minecraft
speedrunner in the world right now.”
“I guess,” Oscar yawns. “Maybe you should count yourself lucky I didn’t have the guts to go
through with karting properly. I one hundred percent would’ve kicked your ass.”
“You absolutely would not have,” Lando laughs. “I’m actually also really good at what I do.”
“I know,” Oscar says immediately, sounding fond in a way that makes warmth unfurl
annoyingly through Lando’s chest. “I don’t stan losers.”
“Though technically,” Lando says, “I did lose.”
“You would’ve won if Gabriel hadn’t gone against team orders,” Oscar replies without
hesitation. “Those points were yours. Every sensible teammate would’ve given the place
back.”
Lando grins helplessly at that. “You’re only saying that because I’ve successfully
indoctrinated you into my anti-Bortoleto agenda.”
“Maybe,” Oscar admits. “And because I pity you a little bit.” His voice has gone droopy
around the edges again, softer and slower now.
“Are you falling asleep?” Lando asks, grinning. “I should probably hang up before you
accidentally start confessing your deepest secrets to me and then panic about it tomorrow and

ghost me forever.”
“You understand me disturbingly well,” Oscar mutters, and there’s something strangely
sincere buried underneath the joke. “I don’t like it.”
“We’re friends,” Lando protests automatically. “Of course I understand you.”
A pause.
“We’re friends?” Oscar repeats, sounding genuinely uncertain about it somehow, in a way
that weirdly almost hurts Lando’s feelings a little.
“Yeah,” Lando says immediately. “At least… I’d say we are.” He shifts slightly deeper
underneath the blanket of shadows pooling across his apartment. “I mean, okay, we
technically only just met, but we’ve spent a ridiculous amount of time together already and I
don’t know if I’m massively overestimating things here, but I feel like we genuinely get
along really well.” A grin tugs at the corner of his mouth again. “Your chat seems to think so
too.”
There’s a small silence. Then:
“Lando Norris,” Oscar says slowly, sounding almost incredulous. “Did you seriously watch
my stream?”
“I had nothing better to do,” Lando says quickly, immediately attempting to salvage the
situation. “And I wanted to scope out the competition. Which, by the way, made me realise I
might actually be completely fucked.”
“Nah,” Oscar says easily, entirely unbothered. “You’ve got a really good aptitude for the
game actually. You’re a fast learner in general.” A pause. “You’re just a little too inside your
own head sometimes. But we’ll work on that.”
Lando scoffs quietly. “I’m inside my own head? What exactly is that supposed to mean?”
“You get tilted super easily,” Oscar says, slipping so naturally into coach mode that it almost
makes Lando smile. “You let RNG throw you off your game immediately, and unfortunately
the deeper we get into runs the more RNG-heavy everything becomes.” His voice softens
slightly again. “But I’ll teach you.”
Lando smiles despite himself. He likes the certainty threaded through Oscar’s voice
whenever he says things like that, the easy confidence with which he speaks about their
future progress as though failure has already been ruled out entirely.
“Okay,” Lando says softly. “We’re going to win this.”
“Exactly,” Oscar laughs quietly. “We’re going to win this.”
A beat.
“Or,” Lando adds, grinning again, “at the very least we’re going to beat Max.”

“Oh, definitely,” Oscar says immediately, and Lando can hear the smile in his voice so
clearly that he can practically see it. “I don’t have the tiniest doubt about that.”
“You should probably go to sleep,” Lando says after a moment, the teasing edge slipping
back into his voice. “What good is a coach going to be to me if he’s cognitively non-
functional from sleep deprivation?”
“You’re right,” Oscar groans softly. “I’ve been awake for, like, thirty hours again.”
“Why do you keep doing this to yourself?”
“No idea,” Oscar sighs. “There’s this persistent English tax-evader who keeps wanting to talk
to me. I genuinely don’t know how to deal with that.” A tiny pause. “Or understand it.”
Another pause. “And I really, really don’t want to stop talking to him.”
Lando’s chest tightens faintly around that, but he brushes over it anyway, laughing softly
instead because the alternative feels somehow too fragile to touch directly.
“You see?” he says. “I told you we’re friends.”
He bites lightly against his lower lip before adding: “You should text your mum. Tell her you
made a friend. Maybe she’ll finally get off your back for a bit.”
“Oh, absolutely not,” Oscar exhales. “She’s just going to panic that you’re filling my head
with foolish motorsport dreams again.” A yawn bleeds through the sentence. “Besides, she
fundamentally doesn’t believe internet friends qualify as real friends.”
“Then we’ll just have to meet in person so it becomes real,” Lando says, and immediately
feels his breath hitch slightly in his throat afterward. “Come to the Melbourne Grand Prix.
Please.”
Oscar laughs quietly at that. “Goodnight, Norris.”
“Osc,” Lando complains immediately. “Don’t hang up yet.”
God, he really is far too clingy. He knows that about himself already – knows how intense he
gets once somebody matters to him even a little, how reluctant he becomes to let
conversations end once he’s settled comfortably inside them.
“I’m going to fall asleep,” Oscar warns him softly. “Like… very, very soon.”
“I’ll hang up eventually,” Lando promises. “Or maybe I’ll just stay here and listen in. Maybe
you sleeptalk. Maybe you’ll accidentally reveal something useful.”
“I don’t,” Oscar mumbles, his voice getting lower and slower now, sleep finally beginning to
drag him under properly at last. His guard feels almost entirely gone suddenly.
“Tell me one thing about yourself before you fall asleep,” Lando says quietly, leaning farther
back into the couch cushions so he can stare up at the dark ceiling overhead. “Anything.
Doesn’t have to be deeply personal. Just give me a fun fact.”

For a moment, there’s nothing, long enough that Lando genuinely thinks Oscar might already
have drifted off. But then his voice returns again, barely intelligible now, rough with
exhaustion and sleep.
“The main reason I became a fan of you,” he slurs softly, “was because I was so fucking
heartbroken about not being able to race that I basically picked somebody to live through
instead.” A pause. “I used to imagine I was you.”
Something in Lando’s chest twists painfully at that confession, so raw and vulnerable in its
sleep-heavy honesty that for a second he genuinely cannot think of a single thing to say in
response.
“You winning in Miami last year,” Oscar continues quietly. Another small pause. “In a way,
I’d won too.” His voice is barely more than a murmur now, words slurring together at the
edges with exhaustion. “I think that’s when I finally got over it.”
Lando’s chest tightens painfully. “Oh, Osc,” he says softly. “I’m really sorry.”
But Oscar doesn’t answer. And after a few seconds, Lando realises why.
The line has gone quiet in that particular way that only sleeping people are quiet, the faint
sound of breathing still threading softly through the speakers of his phone where it rests
balanced against his knee. Somewhere on the other side of the world, Oscar has finally fallen
asleep for real at last, his guard lowered completely for probably the first time since they met.
Lando stays there for a while longer without hanging up. Listening.
He knows this is precious. Knows instinctively that Oscar does not hand trust out lightly, that
every tiny detail Lando has managed to pry from him over the course of the evening has been
yielded reluctantly, carefully, like something valuable being surrendered piece by piece. And
yet tonight, despite refusing him his surname, his face, his degree, despite still clinging so
fiercely to anonymity, Oscar has still offered him something else entirely instead: the shape
of his hunger.
And Lando, for all his impulsiveness and his tendency to bulldoze through people’s
boundaries purely because curiosity burns too brightly inside him, is sensible enough to
understand what a gift that is.


IV.
 
They sit out on the deck of the little yacht a few hundred metres off the coast, the green
island with its jagged cliffs at their backs and the open Atlantic stretching turquoise and
glassy out before them, shallow enough here that sunlight still fractures against the pale sand
underneath the water. 

Pietra is tanning on the sundeck in a tiny bikini and oversized sunglasses while Max absent-
mindedly massages sunscreen into her back or finds any other available excuse to keep
touching his girlfriend; and Lando lies sprawled out nearby with his eyes closed, basking in
the warmth like a cat, his shirt hanging open and his cap turned backwards.
Magui sits cross-legged near the edge of the boat, lazily spitting watermelon seeds into the
sea where they land with soft plop, plop, plops against the surface.
Two days ago, while they’d all been trampling through the grey snow slush coating the
pavements of Monte Carlo in pursuit of increasingly desperate last-minute Christmas
shopping, Pietra had suggested – with the kind of spontaneity only very wealthy people seem
capable of – that they should just fuck off to Madeira for a few days instead. 
The Christmas lights strung between the buildings had glittered above them like some
elaborate visual ambush. Magui had immediately been on board, of course, and together the
two girls had managed to wear down their respective boyfriends enough to pry them away
from their increasingly obsessive Minecraft tournament preparations for a whole forty-eight
hours.
To get some sun. Swim in warm water. Eat good food. Enjoy, however briefly, the absurdity
of living lives where you could spontaneously fly to a volcanic island in the Atlantic just
because Monaco had become too cold and grey for your liking.
“You know what would be really nice right now?” Lando says eventually, turning the cold
bottle of beer slowly in his hand while his voice drifts through the soft music humming from
the yacht’s speakers.
Magui turns toward him immediately, her mouth sticky and red with watermelon juice like an
unsupervised toddler, apparently having once again failed to master the concept of biting
from the sides instead of directly through the centre. “What?” she asks suspiciously.
“Playing Minecraft,” Lando says, unable to suppress the shit-eating grin immediately
spreading across his face.
Magui makes a horrified noise and immediately rips her hat off her head to throw it directly
at him.
From the sundeck behind them, Max bursts out laughing. “Mate,” he says, “you have got to
be kidding me. I was literally just thinking the exact same thing.”
Lando sits upright immediately, pointing triumphantly toward him. “Right? Like, I closed my
eyes and instantly started mentally routing a treasure bastion. I could literally see one.”
“Every time I look at the ocean now,” Max says mournfully, “my first instinct is to dive down
and loot the shipwreck.”
“Or find a ravine with a lava pool,” Lando adds.

Pietra – whom Lando could’ve sworn had been asleep – slowly lifts her head off the towel. “I
fucking knew you were drawing patterns on my leg,” she says flatly to Max. “You two are
genuinely mentally ill.”
“We’re locked in,” Max corrects her immediately. “Super fucking locked in.”
“No,” Magui says, instantly siding with Pietra. “You know an hour ago when Lando suddenly
disappeared and I had to go looking for him below deck?” She points accusingly at him with
a sticky watermelon finger. “Do you know what he was doing?”
“I was merely taking refuge from the sun for a moment,” Lando says with dignity.
“He was watching a Minecraft stream,” Magui says flatly, before throwing the thoroughly
gnawed watermelon rind over her shoulder into the ocean.
Max visibly brightens. “Oh, nice. Which one?”
“Osc’s, obviously,” Lando says, and to his own annoyance he can hear the traitorous fondness
threading itself directly into his voice the second he says Oscar’s name aloud. “He’s training
Lily today since we switched slots so I could actually come here.”
“This trip was literally supposed to function as an intervention,” Magui groans dramatically.
“All you two do is play Minecraft, think about Minecraft, watch Minecraft, talk about
Minecraft. It’s genuinely becoming pathological.”
“I will not be accepting criticism from a woman whose mouth is currently entirely coated in
watermelon juice,” Lando informs her loftily, grabbing the hat she previously launched at his
head and tossing it back at her.
“Oh, merda,” she mutters immediately, trying unsuccessfully to wipe at her face without any
actual knowledge of where the juice even is.
Lando grins and gets up from his chair, crossing the deck before crouching down next to her
and pressing his thumb lightly against the corner of her mouth to wipe the sticky red streak
away.
“Wait,” Max says suddenly. “Stay exactly like that for a second. That’s an excellent picture.”
Magui immediately turns toward Lando with a grin.
Max has always had a frighteningly good instinct for moments like these – candid little
snapshots that could, with absolutely zero effort, be interpreted entirely out of context by the
internet. Especially because it slots so perfectly into the image people already have of them
after years of ambiguity and strategic confusion and the unfortunate fact that Lando once
kissed her three separate times on the corner of her mouth in various paddocks around the
world.
It really is alarmingly easy to fake heterosexuality sometimes. People see closeness and
immediately project something they understand onto it.

Honestly, it’s the first useful thing heteronormativity has ever done for him.
Pietra hands Max his phone and Max immediately snaps several photos in rapid succession:
Lando kneeling beside Magui with his shirt hanging open and his backwards cap, Magui in
her flimsy beach dress with saltwater still drying in her hair from the last time she threw
herself into the ocean half an hour ago, her looking up at him with enormous fond eyes while
his hand cups her jaw.
“Wait,” Lando says suddenly. “I can do you one better.”
And before Magui can react, he leans down and deliberately licks the remaining smear of
watermelon juice off the side of her mouth.
The camera shutter buzzes furiously. Pietra actually recoils.
“You two are genuinely fucking disgusting,” she says, sounding deeply impressed despite
herself as she lowers her sunglasses down her nose to stare at them properly. “Max would
never lick watermelon juice off my face. And we’re actually dating.”
Lando grins shamelessly before pressing a quick kiss directly against Magui’s lips. “We
would’ve been so powerful together.”
“God knew the world couldn’t handle us if we were straight,” Magui sighs, already reaching
back down for her watermelon again.
Lando watches in horror as she immediately takes another gigantic bite directly through the
middle.
“Oh my god,” he groans. “Please stop eating it like that. Don’t you understand that this is
exactly why your entire face ends up sticky every single time?”
She shoves him square in the chest hard enough that he topples backwards onto the warm
deck boards.
“Leave me alone, chuchu,” she scoffs. “What are you, the fucking watermelon police?”
Lando’s phone dings softly from beside his chair and he reaches for it instinctively, unlocking
the display to see that Max has already dumped the photos into their four-way group chat.
He scrolls through them slowly. God, they’re good.
Max genuinely has an absurd eye for this kind of thing – for moments that look effortless and
candid while somehow still feeling cinematic. Especially because none of the smiles are
posed; Magui is genuinely laughing in every single one, her face tilted up toward him while
his hand cups her jaw, and in the one where he’s got his mouth pressed dramatically against
the side of her face while she clutches at his forearms, they genuinely look insufferably in
love.
“Thanks,” Lando says, still flicking through the pictures. “I’m posting these to my story
immediately. Excellent prophylaxis since I was thinking about going to that beach club

tonight.” He grins lazily. “Need a little bit of Magui’s protective spell around me.”
Magui blows him an exaggerated sticky kiss from across the deck and he pretends to catch it
dramatically against his chest while Pietra lets out a delighted little ohohoh.
“Wait,” she says immediately. “Is Lando Norris finally planning on getting laid again?”
Lando throws her the dirtiest look imaginable. “Leave me alone,” he groans, though
unfortunately he can already feel his cheeks beginning to redden slightly beneath the sunburn
warming his face.
Truthfully, it has been a while.
And for somebody who enjoys sex as much as Lando does, the absence of it begins to gnaw
eventually, grinding faintly underneath his skin like frustration without a proper outlet. 
“Does anybody want to dive to the bottom of the ocean with me?” Magui asks roughly ten
seconds later after demolishing yet another slice of watermelon.
“No thank you,” Pietra says immediately from beneath her sunglasses, and Max shakes his
head too, which unfortunately leaves only–
“Come on,” Magui needles him instantly. “You can pretend you’re searching for one of your
stupid little shipwrecks from your nerd game.”
Lando laughs despite himself. “Fine.”
Magui is on her feet instantly. She grabs his hand with her still watermelon-sticky fingers and
drags him bodily across the deck toward the back of the yacht where she immediately yanks
his cap off his head before shoving him straight into the ocean fully clothed.
“Magui, are you fucking kidding–” The water swallows him whole before he can finish
protesting.
Warm saltwater crashes around him, soft and turquoise and shockingly pleasant against sun-
heated skin, filling his ears and stinging faintly at his eyes while Magui cannonballs in after
him with a victorious shriek. Lando resurfaces, spluttering and laughing immediately,
pushing wet hair out of his face while she paddles away from him at astonishing speed.
They swim around toward the front of the yacht where Max is already leaning over the
railing filming them with his phone while Magui repeatedly attempts to drag Lando
underneath the surface by his wrists.
“Oh my god,” Lando coughs after resurfacing for approximately the seventh time. “Stop
trying to drown me.”
And yet somewhere between the repeated attempted murders and the warm ocean wrapping
around him and Magui’s relentless laughter ringing through the air, Lando realises she has,
once again, understood him almost frighteningly well without him ever needing to explain
anything at all.

Sometimes you really do just need to wrestle your friends in the ocean to feel good about
yourself again.
Max eventually throws them snorkels and goggles from the deck – mostly because he’s
decided this entire thing would make excellent content for the little Quadrant vlog he plans
on uploading after the trip – and soon Magui is dragging Lando hand-in-hand beneath the
surface in pursuit of fish and underwater rock formations while Max films them from above.
An hour later, Lando collapses onto the sundeck completely exhausted, water pooling
underneath him from his soaked shirt while the late afternoon sun bakes pleasantly against
his skin. Magui stands over him, wringing seawater from her hair directly into his face with
malicious delight, and in revenge he grabs her ankle blindly, tugging hard enough that she
topples down on top of him with a shriek.
They end up a mess of tangled limbs and wet skin and saltwater laughter, wrestling half-
heartedly against each other until Magui accidentally elbows him straight in the face.
Another hour later, they are all gathered around a bottle of wine on the deck – Lando with a
tissue full of ice pressed dramatically against his nose from Magui’s overly spirited assault –
while Magui and Pietra attempt to teach the boys Sueca, a Portuguese four-player card game
in which Max and Pietra team up against Lando and Magui.
Very quickly, however, the actual game stops mattering altogether. Instead, Pietra and Magui
descend into something that resembles a proxy war more than anything else,
instrumentalising Max and Lando in their increasingly fierce attempts to each establish
themselves as the greatest Sueca player currently aboard this boat. 
At some point they entirely abandon English and begin insulting one another in rapid-fire
Portuguese across the cards while Max and Lando sit there grinning helplessly to themselves,
equally amused by the sheer ferocity of their competitiveness.
They return to the shore after that – Pietra and Magui still bickering fiercely over who
actually won their Sueca game – and briefly head back to the hotel to wash the saltwater off
their skin before wandering back down toward the beachside strip for dinner. It’s their only
proper evening here, after all, considering they’ll already be flying back to Monaco tomorrow
afternoon, and so there seems to be a collective agreement that they ought to make the most
of it.
The restaurant sits directly by the water, warm light spilling out across the sand while the
ocean breathes softly somewhere beyond the terrace. Magui, Pietra and Max order what
appears to Lando to be every available sea creature on the menu while he watches them with
undisguised disgust over his tomato sugo pasta.
At some point during the evening, Magui and Pietra disappear together for a cigarette –
something they both always seem to require the second they become even mildly drunk –
which leaves Lando alone with Max for the first time all day.
“It’s so nice here,” Max groans eventually, tipping his head back in his chair to stare up at the
night sky above them, perfectly clear and crowded with stars. “And still, all I can think about

is how I should be home playing the game right now.”
Lando laughs softly. “Same,” he admits, mirroring Max’s posture to look up at the sky
himself. “Is it weird to say I genuinely can’t wait to get back so I can play more?”
“Magui and Pietra would absolutely kill you for saying that aloud,” Max says with a grin.
“But yeah. I feel exactly the same.”
Lando pulls out his phone again and opens Instagram, idly rewatching the stories he posted
throughout the day: the turquoise ocean stretched endlessly ahead of them; then the photo
Max took of him and Magui – the one he ultimately chose because the angle disguises the
fact that he is very obviously licking watermelon juice off her face and instead makes it look
suspiciously like they are kissing while she laughs. 
He tagged her almost invisibly in the corner and added a tiny white heart over the image for
maximum effect.
Then comes the video Max took of him and Magui diving for shells; another of him climbing
back onto the boat afterward with his soaked shirt plastered transparently against his skin.
That one is objectively a thirst trap, Lando has to concede privately. But in his defence, it is
also just a genuinely excellent picture.
He tabs over to Oscar’s Instagram chat to see whether he reacted to any of the stories, only to
discover instead that Oscar has tagged him in his story roughly an hour ago.
Immediately, Lando opens it.
It’s a photo of the enormous black PR box sitting on what appears to be Oscar’s kitchen table,
already ripped open to reveal the frankly absurd amount of McLaren, LN4 and Quadrant
merch stuffed inside.
Over it, Oscar has written: cheers @lando, you narcissist
Lando grins so hard his face genuinely starts hurting. Instantly, he replies.
 

lando
Mate, send me a picture of youuuuuu in one of the jerseys pleaaaase

 
Then, because he fundamentally cannot help himself, he tabs over to Twitter to gauge the
reaction to the day’s stories and is immediately assaulted by approximately twelve thousand
screenshots of himself.
Predictably, the soaked white shirt picture has absolutely annihilated people’s composure.

One viral tweet compares him directly to Colin Firth emerging from the lake in the 1995
Pride and Prejudice, alongside several side-by-side images of that gay guy from Bridgerton
dramatically staring yearningly into middle distance while damp.
Lando snorts aloud at the comparison. But then his eyes snag farther up the timeline on
another tweet entirely from the same account.

GUYSSSSS OP (the minecraft guy lando streams with) LIKED AND THEN UNLIKED
MY POST ABOUT LANDO X ANTHONY BRIDGERTON X DARCY HAHAHAHAHAHA

Attached beneath it sits a screenshot for proof. The replies underneath are already losing their
collective minds.
Butter fingers, Lando knows them well. But at least it proves his theory that Oscar’s Twitter
timeline is apparently full of Lando content – exactly the same way Lando’s own timeline
has, over the last week, become increasingly infested with Oscar.
There are already tweets about Oscar’s Instagram story too. The general consensus seems to
be that everyone’s suspicions have been entirely correct: OP81 and Lando Norris get along
alarmingly well, to the point where Lando is apparently sending him personalised merch
packages now, and Oscar’s caption only further suggests a sort of easy familiarity between
them that people online have immediately sunk their teeth into.
One particular tweet catches Lando’s eye.

I AM SO SO SICK OF PRETENDING LIKE I DON’T FUCKING SEE IT. I KNOW
Y’ALL OPBERG AND CARLANDO SHIPPERS ARE GONNA COME FOR MEEE but
Lando’s genuinely out there sending his fanboy merch packages like a sugar daddy. I
WILL NOT BE SILENCED. taking shipname suggestions btw

Lando snorts into his wine before locking his phone again. Some of his fans genuinely live in
an entirely different reality.
Especially considering the fact that he literally spent the entire day posting suspiciously
couple-coded pictures with Magui – pictures which, judging by the rest of the timeline,
people have also enthusiastically latched onto with endless awwws and heart emojis and
declarations that they are so clearly in love.
“I was wondering something,” Max says eventually while Lando puts his phone down on the
table and reaches instead for his wineglass.
“Hm?”
“How does the ninjabrainbot thing actually work?” Max asks, sounding almost embarrassed
by the question. “Couri basically just told me it’s legal and showed me how to read it, but I
still fundamentally don’t understand what’s happening.”
Lando bursts out laughing. “Did you seriously spend the last five minutes staring at the stars
and pondering stronghold triangulation?”

“Yeah,” Max groans, dragging a hand through his hair. “God, this game has genuinely broken
my brain.”
“Osc explained it to me really well actually,” Lando says, and before Max can reply he gets
up from his chair and drops down into the seat beside him instead. He grabs one of the little
promotional flyers lying on the table alongside the pen Magui used earlier to write a postcard
home to her family, then flips the paper over and starts sketching on the back while Max
leans closer.
“So look,” Lando says, drawing two dots connected by a crooked line. “Here’s the
stronghold, right? And here’s you.”
He taps both points with the pen.
“That’s why you throw two Eyes of Ender. The first one gives you the angle, then you run
four sprint jumps forward and throw the second eye.” He draws another line. “And from the
angle difference between those two throws you can calculate the overworld distance.” He
pauses briefly, trying to remember the exact phrasing Oscar used. “It’s basically just… those
maths problems we did in school with the triangles.” He grins. “Triangulation.”
Max looks at him with a deep frown. “How the fuck do you know these things? Genuinely.
How does Lando Norris sit here and casually utter words like angle and triangulation. Has
hell frozen over?”
Lando leans back in his chair, a smug smile tugging immediately at the corner of his mouth.
“I have an excellent fucking coach.”
His best friend squints at him suspiciously. “He must really be worth his salt if he managed to
make you understand maths.”
“I love listening to him explain things to me,” Lando admits, and annoyingly enough he can
already feel the smile softening his entire face the second he starts talking about Oscar. “Like,
streaming with him is fun obviously, but honestly I think I like talking to him off-stream the
most.”
“Huh,” Max says.
“What?”
“Nothing.” Max turns the wineglass slowly between his fingers before glancing sideways at
him again. “Uh… how much time do you actually spend on call with him exactly? Because
I’ve noticed your calls to me have dropped off dramatically.”
Lando does the maths in his head. “We usually stay on the phone after stream,” he says
slowly. “Like after we’re done training or after he finishes coaching Lily. And then we
basically stay on call until one of us falls asleep.”
Max blinks at him.
“So…” He raises both eyebrows. “Like six hours a day minimum?”

“Well,” Lando says defensively. “Not minimum. Sometimes less.”
“Not including the actual streams.”
“Yeah,” Lando says. And now that he hears himself say it aloud, it does sound like kind of a
lot.
“And who exactly initiates these calls?”
“It’s not like we initiate them,” Lando says immediately. “We just… happen to want to talk to
each other and eventually one of us calls.”
Max exhales slowly through his nose. “That genuinely doesn’t strike you as strange?”
Lando frowns immediately. “Strange how?”
Max doesn’t answer straight away.
“How much do you actually know about him?” he asks instead.
And suddenly, annoyingly, Lando feels a little self-conscious.
“Not loads,” he admits. “He tells me little things here and there, but I still don’t know what
he looks like or exactly where he lives or what he really does outside of Minecraft.”
Max stares at him. “How the fuck do you talk to someone for that many hours and not find
that stuff out?”
“I don’t know,” Lando says, more defensively now. “I guess we just focus on different
things.”
“Like what?”
Lando puffs out his cheeks. “Why are you being weird about this?”
“Weird?”
“Like territorial,” Lando says, a crease forming between his brows now. “And jealous.” He
rolls his eyes. “We’re friends, Max. We just get along really well. But he’s obviously not
you.” A pause. “Besides, half the time when I called you recently you acted annoyed anyway.
You’re literally the one who keeps telling me to get a boyfriend.”
“Yeah,” Max says slowly, chewing briefly against the inside of his lip. “Which is why I’m
asking whether you’re maybe, like… romantically interested in him.”
Lando snorts immediately. 
“Max, I don’t even know what he looks like.” He shakes his head. “I just really enjoy talking
to him. He’s genuinely one of the best conversationalists I’ve ever met, and he makes
everything sound interesting.” He stares briefly down at the flyer still covered in crooked

Minecraft maths. “And you know how obsessed I get with analysing people. He’s so cagey
about everything that talking to him actually feels like a challenge.”
Max sighs eventually, leaning farther back in his chair.
“Fine. Sorry for interrogating you.” He shrugs slightly. “I guess I just don’t love the fact that
I can’t vet the guy at all, you know?”
Lando immediately reaches over and squeezes his shoulder.
“You don’t need to vet anything,” he says softly. “I promise it’s not like that.” A small smile
tugs at his mouth. “Honestly, I think it’s kind of healing for me to just… talk to a guy and
become friends with him for once without immediately overcomplicating everything.”
Max reaches up and squeezes Lando’s hand briefly where it rests on his shoulder. “Good,” he
says. “I’m genuinely happy to hear that, Lan.”
“Are you fucking kidding me?” Magui’s voice cuts through their conversation as she and
Pietra return to the table, carrying the faint scent of cigarette smoke and sea air with them.
She stares directly at Lando in disbelief. “We leave for, like, ten minutes and you fucking
nerds immediately start talking about Minecraft again.”
Pietra leans over the table with a grin and snaps a picture of the back of the flyer, all covered
in crooked lines and little dots and incomprehensible geometry, Max and Lando still bent
over it shoulder to shoulder.
“I’m exposing how unbelievably nerdy you both are,” she declares as she drops back into the
chair Lando abandoned earlier, while Magui takes her old seat again.
“Tag me,” Lando says immediately. “I need to flex on my coach that I actually understood
what he was trying to drill into me.”
At that, Max throws him another one of those long, unreadable sideways glances – but Lando
very pointedly ignores it while Magui steals the paper out of his hands instead, tilting it back
and forth like she’s trying to decipher ancient scripture.
“You’re insane,” she says finally. “Why are you doing maths on holiday?”
“It’s maths that helps us find the stronghold faster,” Lando replies matter-of-factly. “Which is
kind of the entire point of speedrunning.”
Magui picks up her wineglass and takes a long sip.
“I’m so fucking glad I’m not actually dating you,” she sighs dramatically as she sets the
empty glass back onto the table.
“You couldn’t handle me anyway,” Lando shoots back immediately, blowing her a kiss across
the table.

She catches it lazily between two fingers and pretends to toss it overboard. Lando pouts at
her in betrayal.
“Honestly,” Pietra says while she edits the story, “I’m beginning to think it’s actually kind of
sexy.” She glances up. “Like… nerdy guys are hot, aren’t they?”
“Oh, absolutely,” Lando says instantly – much too quickly, judging by the way Max nearly
chokes on his wine beside him. “Like when someone explains something to you that you
fundamentally know you’ll never fully understand, but they’re so serious and passionate
about it that you kinda just want to keep listening to them forever.”
Max coughs awkwardly into his fist and suddenly becomes deeply invested in staring at the
ocean instead of contributing to the conversation.
“Story posted,” Pietra announces a moment later. “Lando tagged. Go impress your coach.”
Lando grins lazily as he reaches for his phone lying on the table. God, he’s really been
posting a lot lately. Usually he only gets this active online when he has a crush he’s trying to
impress – but there’s absolutely nothing like that going on right now, obviously.
Pietra’s story is genuinely excellent. It’s a candid snapshot of him and Max bent over the
flyer between them, the jagged lines and arrows clearly visible between their hands while the
restaurant lights spill gold over the table.
Over it, Pietra wrote: magui and i leave for 10 min and those two nerds immediately start
talking about minecraft again… midoffs u better treat these guys well <3
“Nawww,” Lando says while reposting it onto his own story. Then he glances sideways at
Max with a grin. “I’m still beating your boyfriend though.”
“Yeah, please eliminate him quickly,” Pietra says, nudging Max’s leg with her foot
underneath the table. “I need him back. I genuinely can’t take this anymore.”
Lando grins at that. He’s definitely tagging Oscar in the repost. Credit where credit’s due. 
He adds his own caption over Pietra’s story before posting it again. thxxx to the best coach.
go subscribe to @op81 nowww
Then he drops his phone face down onto the table again and reaches for the wine bottle,
topping both his and Magui’s glasses back up.
“Do you want to go to the beach club later?” he asks her while she folds his carefully drawn
triangulation maths into a paper airplane with horrifying disregard for the scientific process.
“Sure,” Magui says easily, squinting one eye shut while she aims the paper plane toward the
lantern hanging above them. “I’m going to be the best wingwoman in the entire world.”
“We’re going back to the hotel after this,” Pietra announces meanwhile after having what
appears to be an entire silent conversation with Max consisting exclusively of eyebrow raises
and tiny mouth twitches. “I’m exhausted.”

Magui and Lando exchange a very long look. “Yeah,” Lando says slowly. “Sure. Exhausted.”
He giggles. “You guys know you genuinely do not need to perform this theatre for us
anymore, right? We’re fully aware neither of you are planning to sleep.”
Max groans immediately. “Please stop being vulgar.” But there’s a lovely flush spreading
over his cheeks that Lando absolutely delights in causing.
Lando sighs dramatically and finishes off the rest of his wine. “This is deeply unfair,” he
laments. “Max and Pietra are going to get laid, Magui physically recoils at the very concept
of sex, and somehow I’m the only one left freezing in the cold.”
“No worries, chuchu,” Magui says brightly, lifting her glass toward him. “I have literally
never failed as a wingwoman.”
They part ways not long after that.
Pietra and Max disappear first, wrapped around each other so closely they almost move as
one person, Pietra already tugging lazily at the collar of Max’s shirt while they make their
way back over the wooden planks toward the hotel. Magui and Lando, meanwhile, wander in
the opposite direction along the beach, toward the exclusive club at the very end of the
shoreline from where the bass already throbs through the sand in soft vibrations underneath
their feet.
Magui has her arm looped around his waist, and every couple of metres she pauses to crouch
down and pick up another shell before discarding the previous one with immense
dissatisfaction. She’s genuinely like a magpie; constantly collecting tiny things only to
abandon them again seconds later. She’s probably going to glue whichever survives this
process into one of her strange trash-journal art projects later.
Lando adores her.
By the time they reach the entrance, the bouncer lets them through without so much as
glancing twice. He knows them already. Lando comes here often enough – usually with
Magui, sometimes with other friends, sometimes simply because he likes the anonymity of
loud music and dark beaches and people too drunk to register who he is properly.
The music hits him instantly anyway, vibrating painfully through his ribcage, but at least the
club is mostly open-air; no suffocating heat trapped beneath ceilings, only salt air and
cigarette smoke drifting in from the ocean.
Magui drags him straight toward the bar.
“Two vodka sours,” she tells the bartender before immediately swivelling around on her
stool, elbows propped against the counter as she scans the crowd with terrifying focus.
Lando knows this is genuinely her favourite part of their arrangement.
“What about that guy?” she yells directly into his ear a moment later, pointing toward a dark-
haired man standing farther down the beach section with two women. “He’s been staring at

you since we walked in.”
Lando follows her gaze.
The guy looks vaguely like Carlos Sainz at first glance – same dark hair, same sort of soulful
eyes – which initially fills Lando with instinctive discomfort. But on second glance the
resemblance dissolves almost entirely, leaving only the soft hair and a sort of adorably
bewildered expression behind.
And yeah, okay, he’s definitely staring.
Not in the way straight men stare at celebrities either. Lando’s long since become excellent at
distinguishing fascination from actual interest; at recognising the particular sort of eye
contact that says I know exactly what you are implying here.
When Lando looks over, the man doesn’t even try to hide it. Cute.
“Yeah,” Lando yells back to Magui over the music. “That could work.”
“Perfect,” she beams immediately, delighted at having succeeded on her very first attempt.
“I’ll soften him up and send him over.”
The bartender slides their drinks across the counter. Magui snatches hers up and immediately
disappears into the crowd toward the little trio. Lando leans back against one of the thick
wooden support beams of the bar roof, sipping from his vodka sour while he watches her
work.
His two female friends absorb Magui almost instantly, laughing and gesturing wildly while
she points subtly back toward Lando once or twice. Meanwhile the guy keeps sneaking
glances over at him in a way that grows increasingly less subtle with every passing second.
Lando waits for Magui’s signal. Then suddenly his phone vibrates in the pocket of his shorts
against the wooden beam.
Absent-mindedly, he pulls it out. A Discord notification from Oscar. And – surprisingly – a
picture attachment.
Lando blinks. Curious, he taps the image.
It loads for barely half a second before it fully resolves on-screen – and immediately Lando
slams his phone face-down against the sticky bar top hard enough that the bartender glances
over in alarm.
“Oh my god,” he breathes. His hand stays firmly pressed over the phone as though physically
restraining himself from looking again.
Underneath his trembling fingers, the phone vibrates again – another message from Oscar
arriving only seconds later.

For one deeply pathetic moment, Lando genuinely considers turning his phone off entirely
and throwing it into the fucking ocean. Because he’s already seen enough.
Enough for his brain to completely short-circuit the instant the image loaded; enough for his
entire body to react before his mind could even catch up.
And now he has to look again. Urgently. Compulsively.
So he picks the phone back up from the sticky bartop, the screen already dark from inactivity,
and unlocks it with fingers that suddenly feel weirdly clumsy against the display.
The picture is still there at the bottom of the chat. Slightly blurry. Clearly rushed. But
devastatingly, undeniably, tangibly real.
It’s the McLaren jersey – his McLaren jersey, bright papaya orange and stamped with the
number four across the chest – except the problem is that the body underneath it is
objectively far too broad and muscular for a shirt that hangs comfortably loose on Lando
himself.
The fabric stretches across Oscar’s shoulders obscenely well.
Not bodybuilder huge, not ridiculous – just solid in a way Lando absolutely did not
anticipate; arms thick beneath pale skin, muscle shifting underneath the jersey where Oscar’s
holding the phone up high enough to crop his face entirely out of frame. There are freckles
and tiny moles scattered across the exposed skin of his forearm and throat, and just above the
collar there’s the sturdy line of his neck, the hollow at the base of it pronounced in the low
kitchen light.
And Jesus Christ. Lando realises with sudden, painful clarity that Oscar outright lied to him.
He is not some scrawny little gamer nerd. He’s a buff fucking nerd. A buff fucking nerd with
absurdly nice arms.
The follow-up message underneath the image almost kills him outright.
