Lando inhales sharply. Then exhales again.
His heartbeat suddenly feels sharp inside his chest, almost painful in its intensity, like every
pulse has developed edges capable of cutting clean through him. Around him the club seems
to dissolve into something distant and muffled, bass softened beneath the violent rushing

sound of blood in his ears while he collapses harder against the wooden support beam behind
him.
Because if Lando is doing the maths correctly – and suddenly he’s very interested in maths –
then if his own jersey size fits Oscar tight, Oscar could probably fold him in half without
much effort.
One and a half times his size, easily – and Lando’s already pretty lean and defined himself.
Which suddenly also explains why Oscar sounded so fucking amused when Lando claimed
he could easily beat him in a fight.
His fingers hover uselessly over the keyboard, incapable of producing anything even
remotely witty.
Usually, banter with Oscar comes easy – effortless little volleys back and forth, something
teasing, something light. But right now every possible reply in Lando’s head short-circuits
before it even fully forms, because the only coherent thought currently left in his brain is
simply: oh my god.
Unfortunately, before he can settle on anything at all, a shadow falls across him. Lando looks
up.
It’s the guy from across the bar – Portuguese Not-Carlos – clearly sent over now by Magui
after whatever matchmaking feat she pulled off over there.
Honestly, Lando’s almost grateful for the interruption. It gives him an excuse to shove the
phone straight back into his pocket and leave Oscar hanging for a moment longer.
“Olá,” the guy says with a grin.
“Hi,” Lando replies, staying leaned against the post, forcing himself to tilt his head back
slightly to properly look at him.
Yeah. Okay. He’ll do just fine.
“I wanted to ask if I could buy you a drink,” the man says, accent soft around the edges of his
English. Then his eyes flick down to Lando’s glass. “But I see you’re already adequately
supplied.”
“Yeah,” Lando says, cocking his head. “But I can buy you one.”
The grin he gets in return is immediate. “Sure,” Portuguese Not-Carlos says, eyes dipping
briefly toward Lando’s mouth in a way that feels promising. “I’ll have whatever you’re
drinking.”
Lando turns toward the bartender again and orders another vodka sour, leaning both hands
against the sticky counter while his pulse still refuses to settle back into anything resembling
normal.

What the fuck is wrong with him? Seriously.
He’s finally gotten exactly where he wanted to be tonight: standing in a beach club in
Madeira with a handsome dark-haired man openly looking at him like he’d very much want
to devour him whole.
Exactly Lando’s type. And yet, despite all of that, his brain immediately betrays him.
Because the second he glances at his arms resting against the bar, his thoughts involuntarily
compare them to Oscar’s.
Not as broad. Not as strong-looking. Not nearly enough like they could fold Lando in half
without effort.
Deeply disappointing, honestly.
The bartender slides the second drink over much too quickly for Lando’s liking, forcing him
to turn back fully toward his intended hookup instead of spiralling over a blurry photograph
of his Minecraft coach’s biceps.
God, he genuinely needs to get a grip.
“What’s your name?” Lando asks finally, leaning back against the wooden post again while
letting his eyes lazily trace the line of the man’s throat.
No moles. Less pronounced collarbones. Oscar’s neck had–
“Rafael,” the guy says. “And you’re…?”
Lando grins immediately. “You’re being coy now, Rafael.”
Rafael laughs softly. “Fine. Lando.”
And then he does exactly what men always do once they realise who they’re speaking to: he
looks him over carefully, openly appreciative, eyes lingering on his frame and hands and
mouth in ways that tell Lando he already knows exactly why this conversation is happening.
Lando lets himself be admired. 
“What do you do?” he asks casually, taking another sip from his drink.
“I work in consulting.”
Lando almost physically recoils. Of course he fucking does. Every single man he meets either
works in consulting or finance. It’s apparently the law.
“Nice,” he says anyway, because realistically how important can PowerPoint proficiency
really be once someone is balls-deep inside you. “You good at it?”

“I like to think so,” Rafael replies, leaning slightly closer against the post so he can hear him
better over the music. His breath smells faintly of alcohol and mint.
“Do you play Minecraft?” Lando asks automatically.
Immediately he wants to throw himself directly into the Atlantic Ocean. What the fuck was
that. Genuinely. What is happening to him.
“Minecraft?” Rafael repeats, visibly confused. “What’s that?”
Lando squeezes his eyes shut briefly and waves a dismissive hand. “Forget it,” he says
quickly. “Doesn’t matter.”
God. He’s actually a lost cause. 
Then he nods toward the darker stretch of beach farther away from the speakers and crowd.
“Do you want to go walk down there for a bit?” he asks. “Somewhere we can actually hear
each other without screaming?”
Rafael’s grin widens instantly – clearly understanding exactly where this is probably headed.
“I’d love to,” he says.
He follows Rafael out through the side entrance of the club, stepping over the little wooden
fence that separates the crowded beach bar from the darker stretch of palms farther down the
shore. Behind him, he catches one last glimpse of Magui standing with Rafael’s friends,
already fully absorbed into their little group, winking at him before she turns back around
laughing.
Then the darkness swallows them.
The little palm grove muffles the music almost instantly, until only the bass remains
somewhere far behind them, soft and distant beneath the sound of the ocean. By the time they
reach the empty stretch of sand beyond the trees, the stars are fully visible overhead again,
scattered brilliantly across the sky.
Lando drops down into the sand first and Rafael follows suit beside him, pressing his drink
halfway into the sand between them.
“I don’t actually want to talk,” Lando admits after a moment.
Rafael grins immediately, like this was exactly the answer he’d been expecting.
Lando sighs. “Unfortunately,” he says, already fishing his phone from his pocket again, “you
do have to sign something before this goes any further. I know that’s kind of a mood killer,
but–”
“It’s fine,” Rafael says easily. “I work in consulting. I love signing things.”

Lando snorts at that despite himself. He opens the encrypted folder on his phone, very
carefully angled away so Rafael cannot see the frankly absurd number of already signed
NDAs sitting there like a collection. He then hands him his phone.
Rafael scrolls through it quickly before throwing him a sideways glance. “You genuinely
have to do this every time?”
“Yep,” Lando says simply, taking another sip of his drink while he looks out at the ocean
instead.
Right here, it feels even more ridiculous. Sitting in front of something as vast and ancient as
the sea while asking another man to legally promise not to expose him afterward just because
of the gender they both happen to be. Against the enormity of nature, social norms suddenly
feel embarrassingly flimsy and manmade; arbitrary little rules people kill themselves
upholding.
“Done,” Rafael says a minute later, handing the phone back.
And apparently deciding immediately that enough time has already been wasted, because the
second Lando takes the phone back, Rafael leans in and goes straight for his neck.
“Oh, okay,” Lando breathes out, mildly startled.
Rafael shifts closer until he’s practically straddling him in the sand, more breathing against
Lando’s throat at first than actually kissing it. Lando leans farther back onto his elbows
automatically, exposing the side of his neck to make the angle easier for him, and Rafael
rewards him with a slow line of wet kisses and soft nips trailing downward.
Not exactly life-altering technique-wise. But honestly, Lando is currently underfucked
enough that the bar is sitting somewhere on the ocean floor.
His phone is still in his hand. And then it vibrates again. Discord.
Immediately his pulse kicks back up. 
Don’t fucking look at it, he tells himself firmly while Rafael works open another button of his
shirt with growing confidence, mouth now dragging slowly over Lando’s collarbone.
Seriously. Don’t.
He clicks on it instantly.
Another message from Oscar.

apartment, awake through impossible hours of the night, grinding games until his back hurts,
and then surfing in the early morning because otherwise his body punishes him for sitting
still too long.
“I definitely need to send you shirts that actually fit you,” Lando says after a moment, trying
to steer the conversation somewhere lighter again. “That jersey looked vacuum-sealed onto
you.”
Oscar laughs properly at that.
“My sister stole like half the stuff you already sent anyway,” he admits. “Said it was road toll

Lando files the phrasing away immediately. All the way. Meaning Oscar doesn’t live
centrally. Meaning there’s distance involved. Meaning–
“I’m sending more,” Lando decides instantly. “Extra ones for her too.”
“She’d genuinely love that,” Oscar says, sounding fond in that soft, helpless way he always

“Oh?” Lando grins. “Alternative how?”

Lando laughs softly. “Okay, so she’s definitely an artist.”

“You’re very protective of her, aren’t you?” Lando asks after a moment, lowering himself

him, the Milky Way smeared faintly across the darkness like someone dragged a thumb
through wet paint.
“She can take care of herself,” Oscar says quickly, almost instinctively. “But of course I
worry about her. I think that’s pretty natural as an older brother.”
“You gave up your career for her.”
The silence on the other end of the line is immediate. 
“I wouldn’t put it that way,” Oscar says eventually.
“But you did,” Lando insists, sitting up again, elbows propped against his knees now as the
ocean folds in and out against the shore before him. “I keep thinking about it, Osc. The fact
that you made that choice.” His throat tightens strangely. “I genuinely think that’s one of the
most selfless things I’ve ever heard.”
“It wasn’t selfless,” Oscar says softly. “I just didn’t want my family to break apart. And it’s
not like I was sacrificing myself for strangers or whatever. I needed them too.”
For some reason that makes it worse. Makes something burn hot behind Lando’s eyes so
suddenly that he presses the heel of his hand against them, annoyed at himself for getting

“Osc, stop,” he says. “Seriously, stop arguing with me on this.”
Oscar laughs softly under his breath, but he doesn’t interrupt him.
“It was selfless,” Lando says stubbornly. “You are selfless. You’re a really fucking good

The silence that follows stretches long between them, taut and humming softly through the

Chapter 3: Tournament/Fortress
Chapter Notes
See the end of the chapter for notes

 
I.

 
The run in which Lando pulls off his first Zero Cycle starts off unremarkably enough.
He plays a shipwreck starting seed – for no other reason than the fact that he knows he
performs incredibly abysmally at them and has been cautioned – by chat, but also by Oscar –
repeatedly, that he's going to get slimed off the bat if he doesn't improve. A Blaze lambasts
him off a fortress wall halfway through the run, and Lando manages to save himself with a
well-timed pearl clutch – but it isn't ideal.
The whole run isn't ideal.
It's one he doesn't stream because it's Lily's day. Lily's day to train with Oscar – which he has
running on his second monitor. 
Lando is getting increasingly unnerved by her laugh; as soft and objectively pleasant as it is;
mainly because it usually follows one of Oscar's dry quips. Or, and that one is somehow even
worse – one of his genuine compliments.
Needless to say, Lando's already kind of tilted.
He's been playing since eight in the morning, right after rolling out of bed and exchanging a
handful of teasing messages with Oscar about his day so far. 
Ever since he returned from Madeira, a new sort of naturalness has slipped into the frequency
of their communication. When they are not on call with one another – during stream and then
immediately transitioning into a private call afterward – they text.
Lando's even got his Discord notifications turned on now, no longer banishing them to the
bottom of his notification centre.
The only time Oscar doesn't text him is when he's streaming with Lily.
Lando has realised he performs significantly better when he has those streams running on his
second monitor. He gets his best runs; sub-thirties all around, which is an insane development

friend of hers; something that had briefly been on today’s agenda before Magui came down
with something and Lando realised he wanted to play Minecraft anyway.

Lando freezes mid-step. “What do you mean?”
“Lando,” Max says. A beat. “I think he's making a move.”
Lando immediately drops down onto the couch at that, grabbing his phone as he bites down
harder on his thumbnail until his teeth reach the nail bed. 
“A move?” Lando asks. “Max, what do you mean?”
“He willingly, unprompted, sent you a picture of a part of his body?” It sounds to Lando as
though Max has stepped away from his desk as well, because he can hear a door open and
close somewhere in the background. “And he looked good in it?”
Lando feels himself swallow, his mouth suddenly dry despite having just downed half a can
of Monster. “Well, yeah.”
“You’re not willing to let me have a look. Just for assessment. Are you?”

Lando actually considers it for a moment.
He’s already told Max Oscar’s real name – might have accidentally let it slip the day after
Oscar told him – and he’s never actually informed Oscar that Max technically knows. And
while Oscar hadn’t sent the picture with any explicit disclaimer that it was meant to stay
between them, accidentally name-dropping him in front of his friends feels very different
from willingly forwarding a picture of a man who notoriously wants as little of himself out
there as possible.
“I don’t know,” Lando says, his voice hesitant. “I feel like I’d be betraying his trust. You’ll
just have to take my word for it.”
Max sighs. “Fine. So Oscar sent you a picture of himself, unprompted, in which even
someone with standards as offensively high as yours objectively thinks he looks good.”
“Well.” Lando shifts on the couch. “Yeah.”
“Right.”
“Yeah.”
There’s a pause. “Describe him.”
Lando feels the heat immediately return to his face. “He’s got, like... really big arms.” He
actually tastes blood from his nail bed at that point and forces himself to stop chewing.
“Ah,” Max says, sounding almost approving. “Well, I know you're really into that.”
He seems to think about it for a moment. “Did the existence of the picture change anything
between you? Like, did things become awkward? Or more... intense? Did you give him
feedback on it?”
“I did not,” Lando says, immediately feeling the embarrassment surge in him again as he
remembers the circumstances under which that photo had found him; and everything that
happened afterwards.
He really, really cannot tell Max about it.
As far as his friends know – courtesy of Magui's self-aggrandizing retelling of the night to a
very hungover Max and Pietra the following morning – Lando left the party with the guy
Magui found for him, and everyone had naturally assumed things had gone their usual way;
as they generally do when Lando is DTF.
Max groans. “Man, what is wrong with you?”
“Like, I called him afterwards and expressed my outright bewilderment at the fact that he's
that jacked. You know, I had assumed he was just some scrawny, nerdy, pasty-white
Minecraft-playing geek.”

Lando gets to his feet and begins to stretch, suddenly realising that his legs hurt from sitting
in the same position for so long while grinding the game.
“And to answer your question, no. It didn't change anything. It was an innocent picture – I'm
pretty sure he intended it that way. For all he knows, I'm straight. I talk about Magui a lot,
and I genuinely think the picture was meant as a humorous jab at the fact that, despite being
roughly the same height, we have vastly different body types. You know. Me, the athlete,
somehow being slimmer than the Minecraft speedrunner.”
“Hmm. I see.” Max seems to contemplate this for a moment.
“I still think it's strange that he sent you a picture of himself. You didn't have to beg for it.”
“Yeah,” Lando says.
“When was this exactly?”
“Our last evening in Madeira. When I hooked up with that guy where Magui wing-manned
me.”
There's a brief pause. “Wait. You said you called him afterwards. Weren't you with that dude
from the club?”
Oh, for fuck's sake. Lando feels his pulse immediately pick up at Max's alarming ability to
connect dots. He really needs to be more careful about what he lets slip in front of that man.
“Not for long,” Lando tries to save face, but Max is already onto him.
“Wait. So you blew this guy off to go talk to Oscar some more?” Lando can practically hear
him raising his eyebrows. “You had an actual hot guy in front of you, doing God knows what
to you, and your greatest priority was getting it over with so you could call your Minecraft
coach and wax poetic with him?”
“Uh,” Lando says, done with stretching now and collapsing back onto the sofa. “It's not like I
blew him off. It was actually a really awkward situation.”
“Why?” Max asks.
“I have sworn myself to never, ever tell anyone about this, actually.”
Max clicks his tongue. “Well, you can't preface a story with that, Norris. Now you owe me
the rest. Just for that pathetic attempt at evasion.”
He pauses, as though he's found an even stronger line of attack. 
“Besides, you want my honest opinion. This is the great decider. And I feel like the fact that
you're trying to hide this from me already tells me quite a lot.”
“Okay, fine,” Lando groans. “But only because you're my best friend. And I trust you. But
you do not tell anyone. Not Magui. Not Pietra. Alright?”

“Yeah,” Max says, sounding entirely sincere. “Of course.”
Lando throws his head back against the backrest, staring at the ceiling as he pinches the
bridge of his nose.
“While the dude was sucking me off, I was looking at Oscar's photo.”
It comes out as half a mumble, but Max seems to hear him anyway. There is a deafening
silence on the other end of the line.
“Oh,” he finally says. A beat. “Yeah, that definitely changes things.”
“The dude noticed,” Lando continues, and the memory alone makes him cringe. “It was so
fucking awkward, Max. I want to curl up and die every time I think about it.”
Max makes a strangled sort of sound. “Lando, why the fuck are you like this?”
“I wasn't planning on it,” Lando immediately protests. “It's just that he texted me during the
whole thing and I wanted to see what he was saying.”
“So you picked up your phone while someone was on your fucking dick and started texting
him back?”
“I didn't text him back,” Lando says, deploying his second line of defence. “I looked at his
message, and there it was. The photo he'd sent earlier. I just... dunno.”
“You just let a man suck your dick while you stared at another man's picture.” Max snorts.
“Great job, Lando. You somehow managed to do two men dirty at once.”
“Wait,” Lando says, and he feels the unease creep up inside him. “Did I do Oscar dirty with it
as well?”
“Well, you kind of did. He almost certainly didn’t send it to you so you could get off to it.”
“I didn’t get off to it,” Lando immediately protests. “I just, you know, uh, climaxed while I
happened to be looking at his picture. But those two events had absolutely nothing to do with
one another.”
“You're fucking beyond it, mate.” Max sounds genuinely exasperated. “I cannot believe you
had the audacity to call me all pouty because some mean internet dwellers made you feel
self-conscious about the way you are with Oscar on stream when you've been harbouring
this... this obscenity all along. Sometimes I genuinely ask myself why I put up with you.”
“I didn’t get off to him.” Lando hears himself begin to scramble. “I swear. It wasn't like that.”
“Maybe,” Max immediately concedes. “Doesn't change the fact that you more or less
prioritised a perfectly mundane phone call with him over very real sex with a very real man.”
A beat. “Should make you think, Lando.”

Lando doesn't immediately reply. Instead, he pushes himself off the sofa and returns to his
chair in front of the PC.
On his second monitor, Lily is still training. Lando hears Oscar's voice drift through his
speakers. He can't make out any of the actual words, but he feels like he'd recognise the
cadence anywhere by now; the drawl of his accent, the shape of his voice emerging from the
static.
“So,” Lando says after a moment. “With your additional knowledge, what do you make of
my original question?”
Max sighs deeply. “I don’t know what to make of it, to be honest. You’re incapable of
forming normal relationships with men anyway. They somehow become homoerotic along
the way.”
Lando scoffs. “That’s not even true.”
“It is,” Max says, sounding absolutely convinced. “There’s something about you that makes
men act weird. But that’s beside the point. Oscar’s a special case anyway. He’s a fanboy. You
just need to figure out what kind of fanboy.”
“What do you mean, what kind of fanboy?” Lando swivels in his chair, his eyes fixed on
Lily’s stream on the second monitor.
“Well, is he a super-straight motorsport-loving dude who’s a fan of yours because he’s
envious of the cars you drive, the women by your side, and the watches you wear? Or is he a
fanboy in the sense that he also likes the cars you drive, but it doesn’t exclusively stop
there?”
“Oh,” Lando says. A beat. “What do you think?”
“What do I know?” Max scoffs. “I don’t know the guy. That’s for you to find out. That is... if
you even want to find out. Because I’m still not entirely sure where you stand in all of this.”
“I’m mainly just super confused,” Lando admits. “I spend a lot of time with him. Want to,
too. We text all the time. He’s funny, observant, attentive – I feel like he just gets me. Up
until now, I genuinely thought I was just making a good friend.”
“Hmm,” Max hums. “Do you want to meet him in person? I feel like that could clear things
up real quick.”
“I’ve been telling him the entire time that I want to meet him. That I’ll send him paddock
passes for Melbourne. That we have to link up when I’m in his city.”
“But?” Max asks.
“He keeps blowing me off low-key,” Lando admits. “He changes the subject or gives me
some evasive answer. At first, I didn’t even notice because he’s that good at it, but there are
certain things that, whenever I press him on them, he just shuts down. And meeting in person
is one of them.”

“That’s strange,” Max admits. “If he’s such a huge fan of the sport – and of you – I would’ve
thought he’d jump at the opportunity.”
“I think he really doesn’t want people figuring out who he is,” Lando says after a moment.
“And if I got photographed with some random Australian guy nobody knew the name of,
everyone watching this tournament would immediately know it was him. But, like... I don’t
get why he doesn’t just tell me that.”
“Maybe he doesn’t want to disappoint you,” Max says, and Lando stills. “I think there’s a
part of him that wants to meet you desperately. But he also knows that he probably shouldn’t
risk giving up the anonymity that’s served him very well over the years for someone who is,
essentially, going to drift out of his life sooner or later.”
Lando bites his lip. “I did actually get him to agree to meet me. Under one condition.”
Max sounds surprised. “Yeah? Which is?”
“That I pull off a zero cycle during the tournament.”
Max snorts. “Well. He knew exactly what he was doing when he agreed to those terms.”
Lando tries very hard not to sound insulted. “What do you mean?”
“Have you ever successfully zero cycled before?”
“Well,” Lando says. “Not yet, but–”
“Yeah,” Max snorts, sounding deeply sarcastic. “He might as well have just said he’s never
going to meet you.”
“You’re such a fucking cynic,” Lando says, his eyes drifting back to his second monitor. “In
fact, I’m going to prove how wrong you are by finishing my current run with a perfect zero
cycle.”
Max laughs. “Sure you are, Lando. Have fun.” Lando hears a rustle on the other end. “If
that’s all from you, I’m going to hang up now.”
“Wait,” Lando is quick to interject. “We’re flying home together tomorrow, right?”
“If you’ll have me,” Max says. “Even though I’m a cynic who doesn’t believe in you.”
“I’ll think about it.” Lando hangs up on him before Max can reply, leaning back in his chair
as his eyes automatically return to Lily’s stream. He turns the volume up again to better hear
what they’re talking about.
Thankfully, they’ve actually started discussing Minecraft again. 
Lily is in the stronghold now, looking for the portal room, and Lando listens to Oscar give her
pointers on how to use the pie chart to figure out the right direction. It feels a little bit like
cheating, listening in on the training he gives her.

But then again, it is public. And he’s fairly certain she watches his streams too, taking notes.
Oscar might not care which of them makes it further in the tournament, but Lando and Lily
are each fighting for their own. That much is clear.
Lando manages to get out of the Nether after another two painful minutes, triangulating his
way directly to the stronghold, and he finds the portal room quickly as well. 
He’s lucky. It’s a two-eye, which means he gets to keep two extra pearls for his confrontation
with the dragon.
It does feel a little surreal to him how much better he’s gotten at this game in just two weeks. 
He’s always been a quick learner, especially when the reward is tangible and immediate; and
he wants to beat Lily, if only to move Oscar further up his own ranking than she did. Which
is why he mainly orientates himself by her times, by her splits. 
He sometimes wonders if she knows that he goes through her publicly available runs and
trains the sections where he falls behind with an almost obstinate sort of recalcitrance; the
same way he grinds mini sectors in the sim until they turn from yellow to green to purple. 
It is remarkably similar to perfecting lap times; and Lando has begun to dream about the
game whenever he falls into bed at the end of a long day of grinding, half-dressed, face-first
into his pillow.
He dreams of sprinting towards desert temples, of collecting wood with explosives. He
dreams of the Nether, of killing Blazes and trades that are too good to be true. He dreams of
killing the dragon, too. With one-cycles, mostly, because he’s still never successfully pulled
off a zero.
Oscar appears in those dreams remarkably often. He haunts the skyscape above him, looming
there while Lando treks across the landscape, placing blocks, sorting his inventory. The soft
cadence of his voice follows him into sleep, giving instructions, offering suggestions,
sprinkling in the occasional bit of praise. Always just out of sight.
Lando enters the end at under twenty-seven minutes; a run that would make Oscar laugh –
but it’s a PB for him so far. He hears his subdued laugh on stream as Lily gears up for a one-
cycle, shooting the end crystals atop the pillars around her while she waits for the dragon to
perch.
“Fuck it, I’ll just try,” Lando says to himself, chewing on his lip as he prepares to pearl onto
the correct pillar before building up his own from there. He can only hope that the game
catches on and the dragon starts veering off her route towards him while he prepares the bed
station out of some spare crying obsidian.
On stream, Lily changes the topic again, asking Oscar how many times he reckons he’s killed
the dragon while she effortlessly shoots the crystals atop the pillars.

“Ha, everyone can do that if they use an aimbot,” Lando mutters to himself, even though he
knows perfectly well that she’s simply absurdly precise and almost never misses a shot. He
can only dream of that.
To his utter delight, the dragon’s pathfinding notices him. He checks the coordinates one final
time before placing the first bed – pre-crafted during a stretch of waiting for better trades –
atop the pillar and begins right-clicking.
The first bed explodes with a bang, tearing a significant chunk out of the dragon’s health bar. 
He’s good at this part, placing beds and exploding them in rapid succession. Because Lando
knows how to be quick; in fact, it’s one of the few things he knows how to do exceptionally
well.
And it helps that Oscar always sounds genuinely impressed whenever he kills a dragon just
with beds – that sort of positive reinforcement acts as a multiplier on his motivation.
He misses one placement, slightly fucks up the timing – but in a last-ditch effort, he manages
to catch the dragon’s hitbox with his axe and crits it once. Twice. Until the thing genuinely
dies at his hand.
“Fuck yes,” Lando whispers under his breath, unwilling to celebrate until he’s sure. He
knows he has roughly ten seconds until the dragon returns to perch and finally perishes – the
only downside of a zero cycle.
But that is more than enough time. He dives into the End fountain and waits.
Then he leans back in his chair, hands clasped behind his head, grinning wildly. Ecstatically.
God. It's almost pathetic how excited he gets about finally beating the stupid game with the
grandiose flourish he's been aiming for; but when the dragon perches above him, the death
animation flooding him with XP just as his personal best – 28:23! – is proudly displayed on
screen, he feels a remarkably similar rush to crossing the finish line first.
The adrenaline clouds his head immediately, like it always does, making everything appear
through a faint layer of haze. Lando's hand reaches for his phone, and for a moment he
considers calling Max again, snapping him a picture, gloating a little bit.
Instead, his fingers betray him, scrolling past his messages and onto Discord. Muscle
memory finds Oscar's chat.
